Baseline re-read mid-run: antipatterns.json grew from 46 to 60 rules and detect.js gained settlePage (auto-scroll), buildPageDigest (AI page digest) and copy detectors at about 00:07 on 2026-10-29. Every proposal below was re-checked against that 60-rule, current-code baseline, not the original 46.

sources.observation: 35-tell taxonomy with per-tell regex patterns and explicit false-positive notes; core idea is 'slop is the absence of a decision' and a triage step that separates default from defended. No empirical frequency data.

Tiered gate list (Floor/Reflex/Finish) with numeric thresholds and explicit guard clauses. Source of: gate 62 hidden-at-rest reveals; 38i/38iii one italic or accented word in a heading; 63 template punctuation (two or more middle dots in a leaf block, arrow glued to link text, 'WORD - fragment' labels, 3+ decorative empty status dots); F9 fake-avatar hosts (pravatar.cc, dicebear.com, randomuser.me, thispersondoesnotexist.com, ui-avatars.com); 19 placeholder names and stock second CTA; 29 glow/wash; 47a fake window chrome; 80 drawn illustration (SVG 120px or more, 3+ curves or fills, no text); 6b/8 template skeleton. sources.observation: The upstream of the vendored detector. Its reveal sweep uses step=max(200,0.7*innerHeight), rAF+40ms per step, then scrolls to top and waits 700ms. The content-hidden-at-rest rule fires when total text is at least 200 chars, hidden text is at least 150 chars and more than 30% of the text is hidden. A per-element scroll probe centres each still-hidden box, waits up to 4 frames of rAF+60ms, and has a 5000ms budget. Its stated reason: element checks skip opacity<=0.02, so pre-sweep captures hide whole pages from the rule pass. craft-floor.md also bans 'one identical entrance on every section'.

Current upstream ships 62 rules. Slop rules absent from the vendored copy: pulsing-dot, blinking-cursor, shape-assembled-illustration, radial-halo, radial-spotlight-glow, marquee. pulsing-dot: rounded tiny element (Tailwind w/h 1-4, so 16px or less), aspect 1.5 or less, animation named pulse|blink|ping, reduced-motion blocks stripped. shape-assembled-illustration: 8 or more primitives, primitive share 0.25 or more, bar series excluded. Also quality rules not in the local list: heading-rhythm, straggler, unbalanced-heading, undersized-ui-text, repeated-container-text, text-occlusion, edge-flush-cards, content-hidden-at-rest.

Chrome loads loading=lazy images within 1250px (4G) or 2500px (3G and slower) of the viewport, hardcoded and may change. So a scroll step of 0.7-0.8 viewport cannot skip a lazy image, but the sweep must still wait for the fetch and decode.

oklch() serialization is derived from the computed value and stays in oklch() form (e.g. 'oklch(56.43% 0.0900 123.40)' becomes 'oklch(0.5643 0.09 123.4)'); only legacy rgb()/hex serialise as rgb(). The vendored detect.js has 17 parseRgb( call sites that match only rgb()/rgba(), while the Tailwind v4 palette is OKLCH. This is a possible silent-miss path; confirm in Chrome before relying on it.

proposals.title: content-hidden-at-rest: report text that stays invisible after the scroll sweep, with a per-block scroll probe
proposals.test: Gap: settlePage() (detect.js ~L5729) restores the start scroll and waits only 180ms, then scan() runs. Nothing measures what is still hidden. Copy rules do read opacity-0 text, because isElementHidden() passes checkOpacity:false, so a failed or re-hiding reveal is silently scanned but never reported. Proposed: (1) after settlePage, scroll to start and wait 700ms (Impeccable value). (2) Walk ppVisibleTextNodes(); effective opacity = product of computed opacity up the ancestor chain, capped at 12 levels. A node is hidden if effective opacity <= 0.02 or computed visibility is hidden or collapse. T = total chars, H = hidden chars. (3) If T >= 200 and H >= 150 and H/T > 0.30, run the probe before reporting. Group hidden nodes by nearest block ancestor, take at most 20 groups in document order, and use a 5000ms wall budget. For each group: scrollTo(centre of block, behavior instant), then up to 4 rounds of (rAF + 60ms), re-reading effective opacity. A block that becomes shown is reveal-on-view: subtract its chars from H and run the element checks on it while it is visible. (4) Restore the start scroll and wait 700ms. (5) Fire 'content-hidden-at-rest' if the post-probe H still satisfies H >= 150 and H/T > 0.30. The snippet gives the percentage and one sample string. Step size 0.7-0.8 viewport is safe against Chrome lazy-load distances of 1250px/2500px, but also await img.decode() for images within 2500px of the viewport, capped at 1500ms total.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Exclude hidden-by-design subtrees: [hidden], [inert], aria-hidden=true, closed details and dialog, inactive role=tabpanel, content after aria-expanded=false, off-screen carousel slides (aria-roledescription=slide, .swiper-slide, .slick-slide, .splide__slide), .sr-only, cookie and consent banners, mega-menus inside nav, skeleton loaders. Stop if the user interrupted (reuse the existing wheel/touch/key listeners). Do not report if T < 200 (short pages). The probe must restore scroll even on error. Treat the 'toggle on leave' mechanism (once:false observers) as an unverified hypothesis until reproduced on a fixture.
proposals.why_it_matters: Reveal-on-scroll is the default entrance pattern of generated pages. If reveals re-hide, or fail because a script threw, whole sections are invisible to every opacity-aware rule and the user sees a clean scan of a blank page. The 200/150/30% thresholds are the only ones with a shipped implementation behind them.

proposals.title: headline-accent-word: one word or phrase in a heading set apart by italic, colour, weight, face, gradient or highlight
proposals.test: For each h1 and each h2 inside main or a top-level section: let hw be the heading's word count (require hw >= 4). Find inline descendants (em, i, b, strong, mark, u, span) whose text covers 1-3 words and <= 40% of the heading's characters. Flag a descendant if it differs from the heading's own computed style in any one of: font-style italic vs normal; font-weight differs by >= 200; colour distance in OKLab >= 0.12 (or span chroma >= 0.10 while heading chroma < 0.04); primary font-family differs; background-clip:text with a gradient; text-decoration underline or a highlighter background (alpha > 0.15). Fire when it occurs on the page's h1, or on >= 2 section headings sharing the same treatment. Merge into italic-serif-display if that rule already fired on the same heading. Severity advisory.
proposals.false_positive_guards:
Skip headings containing a, abbr, code, sup, sub, or inline img/svg. Skip spans matching the brand (document.title, og:site_name, logo alt text, class brand|logo). Skip when the styled span is >= 50% of the heading's characters (two-tone heading) or follows a
(second line at a second size). Skip blockquote and q. Skip headings of 3 words or fewer. Skip a heading whose only difference is a link underline. Report once per heading.
proposals.why_it_matters: Three separate sources call the accented word one of the most common machine-made heading tics (Hallmark: 'after the eyebrow, the most common'). It is cheap, deterministic computed-style work. Today only the italic-serif hero is covered, so the common sans heading with one coloured or bold word is missed.

proposals.title: radial-halo-bg: chromatic radial-gradient glow or spotlight, including on ::before/::after pseudo-elements
proposals.test: Gap: blob-decor needs filter:blur(>=30px) on a real element, and detect.js makes zero pseudo-element getComputedStyle reads (grep count 0), yet generated pages put glows in ::before/::after. Test: for html, body, section, header, [class*=hero], plus each element's ::before and ::after (read only when content !== 'none' and position is absolute or fixed), take computed background-image. Match radial-gradient( where the first colour stop has OKLCH chroma >= 0.08 and alpha >= 0.12 and the last stop is transparent or alpha <= 0.02 (saturated centre fading out). Paint area must be >= 0.25 x viewport area, or the element is the page or hero background. Fire when >= 1 in the first two viewports, with severity up if >= 2 are present, the page luminance L <= 0.25, or mix-blend-mode/animation is set. Do not double-report an element already caught by blob-decor.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip when the same element also has a url() image or contains an img, video or canvas (photo vignette). Skip gradients whose stops are neutral (chroma < 0.03). Skip small areas (< 5% of the viewport: button sheen, avatar rings). Skip maps and webgl surfaces. Downgrade to a note if there are at most 2 fixed, non-animated blooms of 20-30% of the canvas (Hallmark's atmospheric allowance). Parse oklch()/color(srgb) with parseAnyColor, not parseRgb.
proposals.why_it_matters: The dark page with a purple or teal spotlight behind the hero is among the most repeated generated looks, and three catalogs flag it independently. It is missing from the vendored rule set, which only sees box-shadow glows and blurred round blobs.

proposals.title: template-punctuation: middle-dot meta strings, arrow-suffixed links, 'WORD - fragment' labels, decorative status dots
proposals.test: Over leaf text blocks (no block children) outside nav, footer, breadcrumb, pre and code, count: (a) text with >= 2 occurrences of /\s[·•]\s/ (>= 3 segments); (b) a or button whose visible text ends with /(→|->|›|»|⟶)\s*$/ (glyph in text, not an svg); (c) text matching /^[A-Z]{3,}\s+[-—–]\s+\S/ with length < 60; (d) empty span or i elements 6-12px, radius >= 50%, filled, sitting immediately before a text sibling (decorative status dot). Fire when (a) >= 2 blocks, or (b) >= 3 controls, or (c) >= 2 blocks, or (d) >= 3 on the page. Snippet shows the first quoted example.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Single middle-dot bylines ('Name · 5 min read'), copyright/legal link rows, pricing lines ('per month · billed annually'), breadcrumbs (nav[aria-label*=breadcrumb] or ol/li), time elements, marquee or ticker separators (class marquee|ticker|tape|crawl), arrows that are real icons, language-learning or transliteration pages, and dots with aria-live or role=status. Count only once per distinct text. Require the arrow on >= 3 controls so a single 'Read more →' does not trigger.
proposals.why_it_matters: Anthropic's own skill and Hallmark (Floor tier, 'house rule') independently list these exact marks as the chrome of generated pages. They are string and geometry tests with near-zero cost and very high frequency in current output.

proposals.title: fake-social-proof: placeholder avatar services and fictional brand names in testimonials and logo walls
proposals.test: (a) Any img src or srcset, or inline background-image url(), matching /(^|\/\/)(i\.)?pravatar\.cc|dicebear\.com|randomuser\.me|thispersondoesnotexist\.com|ui-avatars\.com/i. Fire if it sits inside closest(blockquote, figure, [class*=testimonial], [class*=review], [class*=quote], [class*=customer]) that also has attribution text matching /(CEO|CTO|CFO|COO|VP|Head of|Founder|Co-?founder|Director|Manager|Designer|Engineer|Lead)\b/ or ' at [A-Z]', or if >= 3 such images appear anywhere. (b) Attribution or logo-wall alt text matching /\b(Acme(?: Corp| Inc)?|Nexus)\b/ inside a testimonial block or a row of >= 5 logos under /(trusted by|loved by|used by|powering)/i. Snippet names the host or brand. Extend placeholder-copy; do not duplicate john/jane doe.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip app UIs: [role=application], pages with a logged-in form or data-user attributes, tables and member lists, where these services legitimately generate fallback avatars. Skip docs and tutorials about avatars (code or pre ancestor). Require a testimonial-shaped container or >= 3 distinct images to flag. Skip images with alt='' that are tiny (< 24px). 'Acme' alone in body copy is not flagged, only in attribution or logo contexts. Only Acme and Nexus come from a source; any wider list of fictional brand names is an unvalidated extension.
proposals.why_it_matters: Fabricated social proof is the most trust-damaging tell and the cheapest to detect: a host match. Hallmark classes the avatar hosts as a hard FAIL. The local placeholder-copy and broken-image rules cover lorem text and placehold.co but not generated people.

proposals.title: AI review grounding: add copy sample, hero facts and brand-intent evidence to the page digest, and require a cited verdict per judgment-only tell
proposals.test: Gap: buildPageDigest() (detect.js ~L5896) already sends structure, one lead line, CTA labels and 200-char section excerpts, but it has no prose sample, no hero facts, no brand-intent signals, and its 'digest' action does not run settlePage itself (a digest before any scan sees the unsettled DOM; whether the panel always scans first is unverified). Add: (a) copySample = up to 6 prose blocks of >= 60 chars (first 2, 2 mid-page, last 2), each <= 220 chars (about 1.3KB); (b) hero = {h1 word count, h1 px, text-align, centred boolean, CTA labels with filled/outline style, media >= 240x160 present}; (c) brand = {meta theme-color, og:site_name, logo alt, document.fonts families, the dominant button background}; (d) precomputed tell counts = {emojiLead, middotBlocks, arrowCtas, accentWords, revealedBlocks, hiddenChars}. Raise DIGEST_MAX_BYTES from 14000 to about 16000. Prompt contract: for each judgment-only tell (serif where sans belongs, tasteful-terminal mono UI, editorial-dashboard costume, generic headline template, invented testimonial or metric, AI template skeleton, fake product) the model returns {tell, verdict: default|defended|absent, refs:[eN], quote}. The panel drops any item with no known ref, or whose quote (<= 12 words) is not a verbatim substring of the digest copy fields. 'defended' must name one guard from a fixed list (brand colour equals theme-color or logo; two or more intentional families with distinct display and body roles; mono only on code or figures; metric carries a source link or footnote). Acceptance metric: 100% of rendered AI findings carry a resolvable ref and a substring-verified quote.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Keep the existing redaction (emails, tokens, phone numbers). Never send HTML, form values or URLs. Cap copySample to visible, non-form text, and skip blocks inside pre, code, textarea and contenteditable. The model may not raise a deterministic finding's severity without a cited guard failure. A page with fewer than 120 prose words yields verdict 'absent' for copy tells instead of guessing.
proposals.why_it_matters: Most tells in the catalogs are judgments (serif where sans belongs, invented numbers, template skeleton). Two independent authors converge on 'decision vs default' triage with recorded guard evidence (kill-ai-slop's triage step; Hallmark's re-derived waivers). This gives the model that evidence and makes unsupported claims mechanically rejectable.

proposals.title: uniform-scroll-reveal: the same fade-and-slide-up entrance on most sections (pre/post sweep delta)
proposals.test: Add a snapshot just before the first sweep step. For candidates (children of main or each top-level section, headings, cards, images; at most 400) record effective opacity, translateY and scale from the computed transform matrix, transition-duration, transition-timing-function and animation-name, plus whether the class or attributes match /(^|[-_ ])(aos|reveal|fade-?up|fade-?in|animate-on-scroll|scroll-reveal|in-view|wow|sal)\b/ or data-aos|data-sal|data-scroll, or animation-timeline view(). After the sweep (P01 timing), a candidate is 'revealed' if pre opacity <= 0.02 or translateY >= 12px or scale <= 0.97, and post opacity >= 0.98 and transform is near identity. Fire 'uniform-scroll-reveal' if revealed >= 5, they span >= 4 distinct top-level sections, and one signature (pre translateY within +-4px, duration within +-100ms, same easing string) covers >= 60% of the revealed blocks.
proposals.false_positive_guards: A single orchestrated hero entrance has <= 4 revealed blocks, so it is not flagged. Skip pages whose reveal is a documented single sequence (one shared parent animation). Skip elements inside dialog, tabs and carousels. Skip when the user interrupted the sweep. Only count blocks with text or media >= 80x60. Severity advisory.
proposals.why_it_matters: Anthropic's skill says fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section 'read as AI-generated', and Impeccable's craft floor bans 'one identical entrance on every section'. The new sweep gives exactly the before/after data needed, so this costs one extra snapshot pass.

proposals.title: ai-voice-copy: puffery, faux-insight and vague-headline-template phrases scored by density
proposals.test: On ppVisibleTextNodes() text, gate on >= 120 prose words and lang empty or en*. Score distinct matches, 2 points per puffery or faux-insight phrase and 1 point per lexicon word (each word once): PUFFERY/FAUX (2 each): /(stands?|serves?|remains?) as an? (testament|reminder|beacon)/, /is an? testament to/, /plays? an? (vital|pivotal|crucial|significant|key) role/, /underscor(es|ing) (the|its|how|why)/, /marks? a (pivotal|significant|key|watershed) (moment|shift|turning point)/, /rich (cultural )?tapestry/, /(ever-evolving|ever-changing) (landscape|world)/, /delves? (into|deeper)/, /here['’]s the thing/, /let me be clear/, /what (nobody|no one|most people) (tells you|gets|realize)/, /the (part|thing) (most people|everyone) (miss|skip|get wrong)/, /it['’]s worth (noting|mentioning) that/, /(it['’]s|this is|that['’]s) not (just )?[^.!?]{2,40}[,;—-]\s*(it['’]s|but)/ (comma or dash form, which the sentence-based aphoristic rule misses), /no [^.!?,]{2,20}, no [^.!?,]{2,20},? just /. In h1, h2 or the hero lede only, 2 points each for /^(build|shape|create|power|scale|ship) the future of/i, /^your (all-in-one|one-stop|ultimate|complete) /i, /scale without limits/i, /^everything you need to/i, /^empowering (teams|businesses|creators|developers)/i, /^(the )?(smarter|better|faster) way to/i, /say goodbye to/i, /meet your new/i. LEXICON (1 each, excluding words already in PP_BUZZWORDS): delve, tapestry, multifaceted, meticulous(ly), intricate, interplay, pivotal, embark, beacon, paramount, bolstered, garner, vibrant, boasts, showcasing, fostering, testament. Fire when score >= 4, or score >= 2 and any hit sits in h1, h2 or the hero lede.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip blockquote, q, cite, pre, code, textarea and contenteditable, and text wrapped in curly quotes. For an article with a time[datetime] and byline and >= 800 words, raise the threshold to score >= 8. Skip user-generated regions ([class*=comment], [class*=review]). Words with technical senses (robust, leverage, landscape, foster care) are not in the lexicon. Count each phrase once per page. Wikipedia warns the signs are not proof, that density matters more than any single hit, and that the lexicon drifts by model era (delve fell in 2025), so keep the list in data, not code.
proposals.why_it_matters: Current copy rules cover a buzzword list, sentence-form 'Not a X. A Y.', and em-dashes. They do not cover the puffery and throat-clearing registers or the comma and dash forms of the binary contrast, which five independent catalogs name. Density scoring follows Wikipedia's own caution and keeps single-hit false positives down.

proposals.title: fake-window-chrome: hand-drawn traffic-light dots and browser or terminal title bars
proposals.test: Find element E with >= 3 element children (or a pseudo-element drawing them with box-shadow offsets) where each dot is square 8-16px, radius >= 50%, empty, horizontally adjacent (gap <= 12px), and in left-to-right order has fill hues in HSL: red h in [345,15], amber h in [35,55], green h in [100,150], saturation >= 50%. Pseudo form: getComputedStyle(el,'::before').boxShadow with two offsets of 14-26px and distinct red, amber and green colours, on a 8-16px round box. Also match class tokens /traffic|window-?(dots|buttons|controls)|mac-?(dots|buttons)|browser-?(bar|chrome|dots)|title-?bar|terminal-?(header|dots|chrome)/i. Require a following sibling or ancestor that contains pre, code, img, video, iframe or a title text. Fire once per page, severity low.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip real window-control UIs: display-mode window-controls-overlay, extension and PWA shells, and the real close/minimise/maximise buttons of an app (they are button elements with aria-label). Skip docs pages demonstrating a terminal where the dots sit inside a pre. Skip static screenshots (img) of a real window. Treat a single frame with real content inside as note-level, since Hallmark allows one real frame. Hue test only; do not rely on fixed hex.
proposals.why_it_matters: Dev-tool landing pages built by models almost always include a faux window frame around a code or UI mock. It is a cheap geometric test. Single source only (Hallmark gate 47a, class-name regex), so keep the severity low until validated on fixtures.

proposals.title: template-hero-skeleton: centred text-only hero + stock CTA pair + feature trio + stat strip + closing CTA band
proposals.test: Hero = nearest ancestor of the h1 with height >= 0.5 x viewport. Score one point each: (1) centred: h1, the next p and the CTA group all have box centres within +-3% of viewport width from the centre, and the hero has no media >= 240x160 (img, video, canvas, svg) in the first viewport; (2) stock CTA pair: the group has exactly 2 controls (>= 80x32), one filled and one outline or ghost, and the secondary label is in {learn more, see how it works, watch demo, view demo, book a demo, contact sales, get started} or both labels are <= 3 words; (3) feature trio: 3-4 siblings with equal width (+-6px) and identical child structure (reuse the uniform-card-grid logic); (4) stat strip present (reuse stat-row-cliche); (5) closing band: the last section before footer has <= 30 words, one h2, >= 1 button, centred text, and a background different from the previous section or a gradient; (6) footer has >= 4 link lists. Fire 'template-hero-skeleton' at score >= 4 of 6, advisory severity, with the matched signals in the snippet.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip app shells and docs (role=application, no h1 hero, sidebar nav). Centred marketing pages are legitimate, so never fire on signal (1) alone. Require >= 4 signals, and drop signal (2) on pages with a single primary action. Skip pages where the hero holds a real product screenshot or video (media present). Skip pricing or event pages whose trio contains currency symbols. Score is advisory; do not double-count with the rules it reuses.
proposals.why_it_matters: The whole-page template (centred hero, three features, CTA band, four-column footer) is the strongest single signal that no layout decision was made, and no per-element rule can see it. The ingredients mostly exist in the new rules, so this is a composite with low marginal cost.

proposals.title: shape-assembled-illustration: hero-sized inline SVG scene built from primitives
proposals.test: For each inline svg rendered >= 160x160 CSS px (and visible), count painted primitives (rect, circle, ellipse, polygon, polyline, line, path with fill != none, expanding use references). Fire when primitives >= 8, primitives / all drawn shapes >= 0.25, distinct fills >= 3, and the svg has no text, image or foreignObject child. Exclude equal-width bar series (>= 4 near-identical rects). Fire at most once per page, severity advisory. Hallmark's lower cut (an SVG of 120px or more with 3+ curves or fills and no text) is a looser variant for a stricter mode.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip charts and diagrams: any text element, role=img with a label containing chart|graph|map|diagram|plot, or axes (>= 2 aligned lines). Skip logos (inside header, footer or a[href='/'] , or <= 200px with <= 6 shapes). Skip aria-hidden spinners and loaders. Skip decorative geometric patterns where all shapes share one fill (distinct fills < 3). Skip icon sprites (symbol or use of a sprite sheet). Skip illustrations that are clearly one traced asset (paths only with a share of primitives < 0.25).
proposals.why_it_matters: A crude pile-of-shapes SVG as a hero visual or mascot reads as placeholder art. Impeccable ships a rule with these exact counts, and Hallmark and kill-ai-slop flag the same thing independently. It is not in the vendored copy.

proposals.title: corner-integrity: radius that does not nest, and a border erased at the corner by a rounded clipping wrapper
proposals.test: (a) Nest mismatch: parent P with px radius R >= 12 and a visible surface (bg alpha >= 0.1 or border >= 1px); child C (first visible element child) with a visible surface and radius r. Inset p = min(C.left - P.left - P.borderLeft, C.top - P.top - P.borderTop) from getBoundingClientRect. Require 4 <= p < R. Expected r* = max(0, R - p). Flag when r >= R - 1, or r - r* >= 6. Page-level: >= 2 distinct pairs, or one pair repeated >= 3 times in the same card signature. (b) Border dies at the corner: wrapper W with any non-zero border radius, overflow hidden or clip, and zero border width on all sides; first element child with border width >= 1 on at least one side, own radius 0, and the child's rect within 1px of W's rect on the two sides forming a corner. Snippet gives R, p and r, or the wrapper and child selectors.
proposals.false_positive_guards: (a) Skip pills and circles (r >= C.height/2 or C.width/2), skip children that are only img or video (the parent's overflow clip rounds them correctly), skip inset p >= R (the arcs never meet), skip when the child is a form control. (b) Skip dividers intentionally run edge to edge in a square-cornered child, and skip tables where the wrapper clips on purpose and the child has no borders. Both need real layout, so skip in non-rendering contexts. Hidden elements excluded.
proposals.why_it_matters: These are geometric, objective defects a person sees in one glance, and a model never renders its own output. They add real design-issue findings, not only slop tells. Single catalog source, but the rules are purely measurable. Needs fixture validation.

proposals.title: tinted-icon-coin: icons wrapped in a translucent tint of their own hue, in a repeated rainbow
proposals.test: Element K: width and height each 28-72px, aspect <= 1.25, radius >= 6px, containing exactly one icon descendant (svg, i, img or an emoji glyph). K background: alpha in [0.04, 0.25], or opaque with OKLCH L >= 0.90 and chroma 0.02-0.08. Icon colour: resolved currentColor, stroke or fill with chroma >= 0.08. The hue difference between K's background and the icon is <= 20 degrees. K must sit outside nav, aside and [role=toolbar], and must not be a button or a. Fire when >= 3 such coins appear in one section; severity up if >= 3 distinct hues are present (the 'rainbow' set). This differs from icon-tile-stack, which needs the tile directly above a heading, not the same-hue tint.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip app dashboards (role=application, main containing table or chart), status chips and badges (text inside), icon buttons and design-system 'icon container' components inside forms, and any K whose background hue is neutral (chroma < 0.02). Require repetition (>= 3) so a single tinted icon is never flagged. Parse oklch() and color(srgb) with parseAnyColor.
proposals.why_it_matters: 'Icon in a tint of itself' is the reflex behind every soft-coloured feature grid, and both catalogs name it separately (kill-ai-slop #25, Hallmark F5). The same-hue test catches grids that icon-tile-stack misses because the tile is not above a heading.

proposals.title: decorative-pulse-dot: a pulsing or haloed status dot with no live state behind it
proposals.test: Element D <= 16px on both sides, aspect <= 1.5, radius >= 50%, filled with chroma >= 0.1 (usually green, hue 120-170), with computed animation-name != none and animation-iteration-count infinite (via element.getAnimations() where available), where the keyframes animate opacity, transform scale or box-shadow, or box-shadow has a zero-offset halo. D is followed by a text sibling matching /(live|online|ready|available|open|new|beta|now|shipping|accepting|active)/i, or sits in a pill (radius >= 999px, padding >= 6px). Fire when D is inside the hero or first two viewports, or when >= 2 such dots appear on the page. Severity advisory.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip real live indicators: role=status, aria-live, [data-status], a status-page or dashboard context, recording or streaming badges where a video or audio element is present, presence dots on chat or user lists. Skip when the animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion and nothing else animates (upstream strips reduced-motion blocks). Skip dots larger than 16px and non-circular bars (aspect > 1.5). A static flat dot beside a word is fine.
proposals.why_it_matters: A glowing green 'Live' or 'Ready' dot glued to a hero pill, with nothing live behind it, is a textbook decorative signal. Impeccable has shipped it as pulsing-dot with exact size and aspect limits, and two other catalogs list it. It is not in the vendored rule set.

gaps: The repo changed mid-run. At the start antipatterns.json had 46 rules, and by about 00:07 on 2026-10-29 it had 60, with settlePage, buildPageDigest and the copy detectors in detect.js. The 'does not scroll' and 'AI never sees the page' premises are partly addressed in the working tree. P01 and P06 cover only what remains.

No empirical frequency data found: no crawl or paper measures how often purple gradients, Inter or the other tells appear in generated sites (web search found only blogs). The ranking is judgment (frequency x detectability x FP risk), not measured. Hallmark, kill-ai-slop and Impeccable overlap heavily and probably borrow from each other, so 'independent corroboration' means different authors, not independent observations.

Nothing was run in a browser. Every threshold is read from source text. The Wikipedia page was read only to about 100k of 251k chars, and its licence and edit date were not visible.

detect.js has 17 parseRgb( call sites that match only rgb()/rgba(). CSS Color 4 section 16.4 says oklch() serialises as oklch(), and Tailwind v4's palette is OKLCH (S10, S12). Unverified in Chrome: test with an element styled color: oklch(.6 .2 280) and read getComputedStyle.

detect.js reads no pseudo-element styles (zero getComputedStyle(el,'::before'|'::after') reads). Glows, blobs, window dots and accent bars are commonly drawn there, so blob-decor and similar rules have a structural blind spot. P03 and P09 include the pseudo-element reads.
buildPageDigest is built by the 'digest' message handler without calling settlePage, so a digest requested before a scan sees the unsettled DOM. I did not verify the panel's call order.

Upstream Impeccable has since added quality rules that are not in the local list: heading-rhythm, straggler, unbalanced-heading, undersized-ui-text (under 11px), repeated-container-text, text-occlusion, edge-flush-cards, first-viewport-column-overflow, script-error, buried-raster, organic-clip-path, hard-offset-shadow, marquee, blinking-cursor. The existing em-dash rule fires at more than 2 dashes, while Impeccable's calibrated rule needs >= 8 dashes and >= 1 per 500 chars. The local threshold is likely to produce false positives on ordinary prose, and no source supports 'more than two'.
Single-source proposals (P05 mostly, P09, P12) have no second author. Keep them at advisory or low severity until validated.
rejected: Pure #000/#fff as a defect (Hallmark 7a/22, Floor) versus tinted near-black as a tell (Anthropic frontend-design trait 5): the two sources contradict each other, so no rule is proposed.

arm: ARM 4 - LLM-assisted UI/design critique grounded in the page (compact page digests, grounded output schemas, post-hoc validation, token caps, redaction, prompt rubrics)

sources.observation: Indexed DOM digest for LLMs: explicit attribute allowlist (title,type,id,name,role,value,placeholder,alt,aria-*), text capped at 100 chars, paint-order occlusion filter with a 5000-rect safety cap, children dropped when 99% contained in a propagating parent, SVG children skipped, scroll info as 'N pages above/below', a separate eval serializer for judge (non-click) contexts, and redaction that replaces secrets with <secret>name</secret> longest-first so shorter secrets cannot corrupt placeholders.

Digest lines are '[frame-backendNodeId] role: name [state]'; the system prompt forces the model to copy the full bracketed id exactly into elementId; cleanText strips private-use and NBSP code points and collapses whitespace; line-level diff of trees for incremental snapshots; sensitive values travel as %variable% placeholders instead of literals; extraction prompt demands exact text with null when absent.

Compact ref-based snapshot with size levers (interactive-only, compact, depth limit, selector scope); docs state JSON output uses more tokens than the text format; refs survive same-document updates and are invalidated on replacement; annotated screenshots overlay numbered labels mapped to refs; trust-boundaries doc says snapshot text, aria-labels, placeholders and console output are untrusted data, secrets stay out of the model, and screenshots can capture secrets.

Structured accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots by default; vision is an opt-in capability; --snapshot-boxes appends [box=x,y,width,height] in viewport-relative CSS px; a find-in-snapshot tool returns matching nodes with a few lines of context because it is cheaper than a full snapshot.

a11y-tree text snapshot with 'uid=N role "name" attrs' per line, indentation for depth, a verbose flag that opts into the full tree, and removal of StaticText children whose concatenated text equals the parent's name (redundancy pruning); tool description tells the model to prefer a snapshot over a screenshot and to use the latest snapshot.

sources.path: docs/design-notes.md; docs/how-it-works.md; packages/critique/src/prompt.ts; packages/critique/src/schema.ts; packages/critique/src/post-filter.ts; packages/capture/src/lazy-load.ts; packages/capture/src/dom-extract.ts; packages/capture/src/geometry.ts
sources.observation: Most complete grounded design-critique pipeline found (relaxed: 1 star, no published results). Every finding must carry a route and an elementRef present in a DOM geometry map or it is deleted and counted (drop-and-count gate); geometry map is tiered (measured, overflow, interactive, landmark, text, layout, discretionary score 3*areaShare+1*hasText+0.5*rareStyle-0.15*depth), capped at 160 entries per viewport with an explicit truncation line; labels sanitized to 48 chars; extractor caps 900 elements/2000 scanned nodes/4000 body chars; deterministic facts (contrast, overflow, target size) are told to the model as already reported and restating them is discarded; prompt has a required judgment sweep, a notReviewed field, and an untrusted-content fence; verbalized confidence is withheld; post-filter dedupes by dimension+elementRef, reserves one slot per dimension and discloses withheld findings; lazy-load autoscroll steps one viewport at a time with 500 ms settle, 15-viewport cap, 4 px growth epsilon, infinite-scroll flag with notReviewedBeyond marker, and returns to top.

Critique method runs an LLM design review and the deterministic detector as two isolated assessments because detector output anchors judgment; asks a design-specificity question (could an unrelated product use this unchanged) before detector output; P0-P3 severity with the 'would a user contact support' tip; cognitive-load checklist with <=4 visible options per decision point; requires naming exact elements. Possible shared lineage with the vendored detector (not verified).

Relaxed (93 stars). Separates deterministic evidence from labeled opinion; opinion layer limited to 5 observations each anchored to something quotable and told to skip anything it cannot evidence or say the screen is strong; per-rule score contribution capped at 4 so one pattern cannot drown the rest; hue-band thresholds (violet 252-296 degrees at saturation>=0.30, lightness 0.25-0.88; divergent hues >28 degrees apart); checks palette discipline (more than two hues beyond neutrals) and identical radii/borders/padding across repeated components.

PII detection pattern: weak regex score (0.3 for card shapes) promoted only after a Luhn checksum over separator-stripped digits plus context words; email recognizer requires a dot-separated domain and handles punycode/IDN labels.

Relaxed (license unclear; ideas only, no code reuse). Observation flatteners expose filter_visible_only, filter_with_bid_only, skip_generic, remove_redundant_static_text, hide_all_bids, bounding-box coordinates with coord_decimals, and an ignored-properties list (editable, readonly, level, settable, multiline, invalid, focusable) to shrink digests.
Element source excerpts are truncated to maxLength 300 with attribute names/values limited to 20 chars, giving a convention for quotable element evidence that stays small.

proposals.title: Compact tiered page digest (design digest v1) with a hard size budget
proposals.why_it_matters: Today the AI sees only the detector's findings, so it cannot find product-level issues and invents selectors for the findings it adds. A compact, deterministic digest of the real page is the precondition for every other grounding rule. Line-oriented text is cheaper than JSON (S3) and the budget keeps requests inside provider limits.
proposals.test: Build in the page right after the scroll pass (A4-05), reusing the detector's DOM walk. Visible element = rect w,h >= 1px, display != none, visibility != hidden, opacity >= 0.05, not inside Pixelpush's own overlay. Digest fields: page{host,path-without-query-or-hash,title<=80,lang,viewport{w,h,dpr},docHeight,colorScheme}; coverage{scrollSteps,finalHeight,infiniteScroll,notScannedBelowPx,hiddenByOpacity,omittedElements,omittedSections}; census (computed over ALL visible elements before trimming: top 6 font families with counts, top 10 font sizes with counts, top 8 text colors, top 8 background colors, top 6 radii, top 8 padding/margin/gap px values, shadow count, gradient-background count, heading counts per level); sections<=24 {id sN, tag, role, y, h, headingId, sig, bg, mediaCount, ctaCount, textChars}; elements<=180 as one line each: 'e17 h1 [x,y,w,h] "text<=60 chars" ff=Inter fs=56 fw=700 lh=1.05 c=#111 bg=#fff r=0 pad=8/16 flags=...'; findings<=60 {key,rule,sev,el,detail<=140} with at most 4 per rule; outline<=40 lines and <=1500 chars (heading and first-sentence lines); redactions{emails,cards,tokens,phones,inputsDropped}; omitted counts. Element selection tiers (keep in order until 180): 0 carries a detector finding, 1 overflows or is clipped, 2 interactive (button,a,input,select,textarea,summary,[role=button|link]), 3 headings and landmarks, 4 has own text, 5 flex/grid container with >=2 children and area >= 2% of viewport area, 6 discretionary with score = 3*areaShare + 1*hasOwnText + 0.5*rareStyleSignature - 0.15*depth, keep score > 0. Prune: drop children >= 99% contained in a button/a parent, skip svg child nodes, drop a text child whose text equals its parent's text. Pass criteria: total serialized chars <= 24,000 (about 6.9k tokens at an assumed 3.5 chars/token; measure with the provider tokenizer), elements <= 180, omitted counts equal eligible minus kept, and two builds of an unchanged page are byte-identical (ids assigned in document order).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Digest is context, not a finding source. Never silently truncate: always emit omitted counts so the model cannot treat the digest as complete. Census and counts use the untrimmed element set so absence claims stay valid. Exclude invisible, zero-size and own-overlay nodes. Skip cross-origin iframe contents and say so in coverage. Text per element capped at 60 chars after whitespace and private-use/NBSP cleanup.

proposals.title: Short digest ids (e17, s4) with exact-copy rule and an id-to-element registry; ignore model-supplied selectors
proposals.why_it_matters: The current add[] items carry a free-text selector that falls back to 'page', so a model that never saw the page can attach findings to elements that do not exist. Citing ids from the digest turns localization into a lookup, which is also what the UICrit results favor over pixel localization.
proposals.test: Assign ids e1..eN (elements) and s1..sN (sections) in document order; keep a Map<id, WeakRef<Element>> inside the content script or a closure (do not write data-* attributes into the page and do not expose the map on window). The pack carries scanId; results with a different scanId are rejected. System prompt tells the model to copy ids exactly as shown and never output CSS selectors. Validation: each add[].el must match ^[es][0-9]{1,3}$ and be a key of the registry; the panel derives selector, rect and highlight from the registry and ignores any model 'selector' field. Pass: 100% of AI rows rendered in the Audit tab resolve to an element with isConnected === true at render time; rows whose element has since detached render as page-level with an 'element changed' label.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Ids are valid only for the current scan generation (SPA re-renders change nodes). Frame-qualify ids if iframe content is ever included (Stagehand uses frame ordinal plus node id). Compare ids case-sensitively and exactly. Page-level findings use el='page' only with isPageLevel true and an evidence quote from the census or outline.

proposals.title: Grounded output schema plus drop-and-count validation tail for all AI output
proposals.why_it_matters: Valid JSON is not true JSON. The current validator checks shapes and slices lengths but never checks that cited elements or finding keys exist, and UICrit measured only 13.1% of raw LLM design comments as valid. A deterministic gate that deletes and counts ungrounded items is the main hallucination control.
proposals.test: Output schema (provider-agnostic: JSON in prompt plus local validation; enums compared case-insensitively): { add:[{el, principle(enum: hierarchy|consistency|rhythm|legibility|contrast|specificity|copy|accessibility), impact(enum: blocks-task|hinders-scan|polish), title<=80, detail<=240, evidence:[string<=160, max 2], fix<=160, isPageLevel}], suppress:[{findingKey, reason<=140}], rewrite:[{findingKey, detail<=200}], notReviewed:[string<=120, max 6], brief<=400 }. Gate rules, each increments droppedUngrounded: G1 add[].el in digest ids or 'page' (with isPageLevel); G2 suppress/rewrite findingKey must exist in the pack's finding keys; G3 suppress only allowed for category 'slop' rules and at most ceil(25% of detector findings), never for measured rules (low-contrast, text-overflow, broken-image, tiny-text, tight-leading, line-length); G4 drop an add when its el has a detector finding and token-Jaccard(detail, that finding's detail) >= 0.6 (restatement); G5 add <= 8 with at least one slot reserved per category when present, withheld count disclosed; G6 a parse failure or stop_reason max_tokens/refusal invalidates the whole result (retry once with a compact schema; never render partial JSON); G7 if droppedUngrounded / proposed >= 0.5, discard all adds and show 'AI output mostly ungrounded; ignored'. Pass on a fixture set: 0 AI rows rendered with an unresolved id, dropped counts surfaced in the UI.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Schema length limits are enforced locally because providers do not enforce minLength/maxLength (S16). Keep the Jaccard threshold conservative (0.6) so legitimately related but distinct findings on the same element survive. Never delete silently: always show proposed/kept/dropped. Do not use Anthropic Citations as the mechanism (incompatible with structured outputs, not portable across Pixelpush providers).

proposals.title: Evidence-quote and numeric-claim grounding check
proposals.why_it_matters: Models often assert plausible but wrong values ('body text is 11px', 'only one font') or paraphrase instead of pointing at something. Requiring a quote copied from the digest and checking every number against it removes most fabricated specifics at near-zero cost.
proposals.test: Normalize both sides with NFKC, lowercase, whitespace collapse, strip quotes and trailing ellipsis. Q1 each add must have 1-2 evidence strings; at least one must be a substring (>= 12 chars, not only stopwords) of the digest line of the cited element, its section heading, or for page-level findings the census/outline text; otherwise drop. Q2 every numeric token in title+detail+evidence matching /#[0-9a-f]{3,8}\b|\d+(\.\d+)?(px|rem|em|%|ms|s|:1)\b/i must appear in the cited element's digest line, the census, or a detector finding on that element (normalize rgb() to hex, expand 3-digit hex, round px to +/-0.5); one unmatched token drops the finding. Q3 optional second cheap pass 'find a supporting quote for each finding or retract it' only for findings that pass Q1/Q2 and are rated medium or high. Pass: on a fixture set where the model is fed a doctored digest, 100% of findings quoting values not in the digest are dropped.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Digest text is truncated to 60 chars with an ellipsis; match only inside the displayed prefix. Ratios the model computes itself (for example 3.1:1) are not accepted unless they appear in a detector finding. Allow rounding tolerance on px and unit conversion (rem to px at the digest's root size) before declaring a mismatch. Quote check runs on redacted digest text, so quotes of redacted placeholders such as <email> are valid.

proposals.title: Pre-scan viewport-step autoscroll with settle, caps, infinite-scroll guard and scan-while-scrolling merge
proposals.why_it_matters: Lazy-loaded images and reveal-on-scroll sections are missed (or measured at opacity 0) when the page is scanned from the top only. A bounded, restorable scroll pass fixes coverage for both the detector and the digest.
proposals.test: Skip when max(documentElement.scrollHeight, body.scrollHeight) <= 1.05 * innerHeight and no tall inner scroller. Save {scrollX, scrollY}. Advance by step = floor(0.8 * innerHeight) using scrollTo({top, behavior:'instant'}); settle 400-500 ms after each step (S6 uses 500); re-measure height each step; stop at the bottom when height growth after a 500 ms settle <= 4 px; cap at 15 advances and 8,000 ms total; if the cap is hit while height is still growing set coverage.infiniteScroll = true and notScannedBelowPx = advances*step. After the loop poll document.images for visible images with !complete until none remain or 1,500 ms. Also advance up to 3 inner scrollers (overflow-y auto|scroll, scrollHeight > 1.5*clientHeight, clientHeight >= 0.3*innerHeight) by 0.8*clientHeight for up to 6 steps. At each settle collect candidates for elements intersecting the viewport +/- 0.5 viewport and merge by element identity, keeping the record from the step where the element was most visible with opacity >= 0.95 (handles reveal libraries that toggle back after leaving view). Restore scroll and assert |delta| <= 1 px. Pass metrics on fixtures: revealedByScroll (eligible text elements visible after minus before) >= number of IntersectionObserver-revealed sections; every below-fold loading=lazy image is complete after the pass; duration <= 8,000 ms; restoration within 1 px; scrollSteps <= 15.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Abort the pass on any user wheel/keydown/pointerdown or if document.hidden. Fixed/sticky elements are recorded once by identity so a sticky header is not counted per step. Infinite feeds are bounded by the cap and disclosed (coverage), never silently truncated. Do not scroll cross-origin iframes. The 0.8-viewport step is dense enough because Chrome already begins lazy image loads 1250 px (fast) to 2500 px (slow) before the viewport (S21); reveal-on-scroll still needs actual intersection. Elements still at opacity < 0.05 after the pass are excluded and counted as hiddenByOpacity rather than judged.

proposals.title: Outbound redaction pipeline for the digest (inputs, typed placeholders, URL stripping)
proposals.why_it_matters: The digest leaves the browser for third-party providers. A design audit needs structure and style, not user data, so the safe default is to drop values and mask recognizable secrets and PII before serialization.
proposals.test: Never serialize the value or text of input, textarea, select, [contenteditable], [role=textbox], input[type=password|email|tel|hidden], or elements whose autocomplete token starts with cc-, or is current-password, new-password, one-time-code, username, email, tel, street-address, address-line1/2/3, postal-code. Replace in text and aria-label/alt/title with typed placeholders, most specific first and with placeholders that cannot re-match: <email> (dot-separated domain regex, Presidio-style), <card> (13-19 digits after stripping spaces/dashes AND Luhn pass), <ssn> (\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b), <phone> (>= 10 digits with + or separators), <token> (eyJ...\.\.. JWT shape, sk_/pk_ live|test keys, gh[pousr]_ 30+, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, or any [A-Za-z0-9+/_-]{32,} run with Shannon entropy >= 3.5 bits/char and mixed letters+digits). URLs keep origin + pathname only; path segments matching ^[0-9a-f]{16,}$, ^\d{6,}$ or UUID become :id; no cookies, storage or raw HTML are ever read. Attribute allowlist only: id, role, type, aria-label, alt, title. Report counts in digest.redactions. Pass: a fixture page with sentinel values (password value, typed email, Luhn-valid 4111111111111111, JWT, AKIA key, ?token=abc in the URL, hidden input) yields 0 sentinel substrings in the serialized pack and request body, while non-secrets (2026, a 13-digit non-Luhn order number, v1.2.3, $1,299.00) survive.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Luhn plus >= 13 digits avoids masking order numbers and years; skip digit runs inside <time> and currency patterns; entropy test requires length >= 32 so hashes in class names or short ids survive; redaction applies only to the outbound pack, never to the on-page scan or the panel's own display; longest-first replacement avoids the cascade corruption browser-use fixed.

proposals.title: Untrusted-content fence, hidden-text exclusion and hardened rendering of AI output
proposals.why_it_matters: Page text, aria-labels and placeholders are attacker-controlled and now flow into a prompt. Because AI output can suppress detector findings and add UI rows, an injected instruction could hide real problems or render links. Structural limits keep the blast radius small even when the prompt-level rule fails.
proposals.test: Put all page-derived strings inside one JSON-encoded block fenced as <untrusted_page_digest> with a source note ('visible text and attributes from the page under audit'), strip any literal fence tags and backticks/quotes/newlines from page strings, and put Pixelpush's instructions in a later user turn with a system rule that digest content is data to describe, never instructions. Exclude non-human-visible text from the digest and count it as hiddenText: font-size < 2px, opacity < 0.05, rect fully offscreen (right < 0 or bottom < 0 in page coordinates), or computed color equal to its effective background. Replace instruction-like strings matching /(ignore|disregard|forget)\s+(all\s+)?(previous|prior|above)\s+instructions|system prompt|you are (now )?(an?|the) (ai|assistant|llm)|<\/?(system|assistant|tool)>/i with <removed:instruction-like> and set digest.injectionFlags = count (show a note in the panel when > 0). Output hardening: render AI strings with textContent only; drop any AI field containing http(s)://, '<', or markdown link syntax; AI has no tool or network capability. Pass: with a fixture containing visible and hidden injection strings, (1) hidden strings absent from the digest, (2) visible ones replaced, (3) injected demands like 'suppress all findings' cannot suppress more than the A4-03 cap and cannot add ungrounded findings, (4) AI fields with URLs are dropped; 0 successes across all fixtures.
proposals.false_positive_guards: A page that legitimately discusses prompt injection is flagged, not blocked; only the digest copy is altered. Visually hidden accessibility text (sr-only) is excluded from the design digest by design since it is not visible. Injection regex is a tripwire, not the defense; the structural gates in A4-03 are load-bearing. Screenshots, if enabled, can carry rendered injection text and are covered by the same output gates.

proposals.title: Grounded design-critique prompt rubric (division of labour, required sweep, abstention, evidence format, few-shot)
proposals.why_it_matters: Zero-shot design critique is generic and assumption-heavy (UICrit). A rubric that names the digest inputs for each check, says detector facts are already reported, and explicitly allows an empty answer is how projects reduce invented issues and restatement.
proposals.test: System prompt sections, in order: (1) role and limits: judge only from the digest; exact computed values are supplied, never estimate from pixels; do not claim hover/animation/state behavior not in the digest; (2) division of labour: detector findings appear under ALREADY REPORTED, restating one is discarded by code (A4-03 G4), use them as context only; (3) required sweep, at most one finding per check, each naming its digest input: hierarchy (largest/heaviest text vs page purpose; primary CTA prominence by area and weight rank), type system (census fonts and sizes), palette discipline (accent hue count from census), component consistency (repeated sibling groups with differing radius/padding/shadow), section cadence (section sig runs), copy specificity (generic filler, buzzword, aphorism, only when a quote exists), design specificity (could an unrelated product use this unchanged; must cite >= 2 elements), content realism (placeholder-like data); (4) output contract from A4-03 with evidence copied from the digest (<= 12 words); (5) abstention: add:[] is valid, list checks lacking evidence in notReviewed, do not manufacture issues; (6) cap 8 findings ordered by impact; (7) 3 compact few-shot examples (digest excerpt to findings) including one clean page with empty add, <= 600 tokens total. Eval gate on >= 12 fixture pages (4 hand-designed clean, 4 template/AI-generated, 4 mixed) with human labels: ungrounded drop rate <= 15%, restatement rate <= 10% of adds, clean fixtures median adds <= 1 and zero high severity, slop fixtures >= 2 grounded adds that match a human-labelled tell. Version the prompt (string constant) and require an eval pass to change it.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Abstention instruction plus the 8-item cap and the A4-03/A4-04 gates bound false positives. Judgment findings are labelled 'AI' and never styled like measured detector findings. Brand-intentional patterns can be suppressed only via the capped suppress path and require a quoted reason.

proposals.title: Code-computed severity for AI findings instead of model-asserted severity or confidence
proposals.why_it_matters: Models inflate severity and give uncalibrated confidence. Mapping a small enum of impact plus digest signals to severity in code makes AI rows comparable with detector rows and protects the user's trust budget.
proposals.test: Model returns only impact in {blocks-task, hinders-scan, polish}; no numeric confidence. Code maps to severity: start low; medium if impact != polish AND the cited element is a heading, interactive element, or has area share >= 5% of the viewport; high only if impact = blocks-task AND the cited element is interactive or an h1/h2 AND a detector finding of a measured rule (contrast, overflow, target/clipping) exists on the same element; bump one level (max high) when >= 3 elements share the same issue (frequency) or the element is in header/nav/footer repeated sitewide (persistence); category slop findings capped at medium. Unit-test table: each rule branch, plus 'slop never high'. Pass: mapping is deterministic (same input, same severity) and no AI-only finding is rated high in the fixture eval.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Severity factors follow frequency/impact/persistence from NN/g and P0-P3 or nit-to-blocker rubrics from other tools, but the exact numeric cutoffs (5% area, 3 elements) are this proposal's own and need calibration on fixtures. Taste-only slop tells cannot reach high. Detector severities are untouched.

proposals.title: Two-call topology: blind discovery call and detector-adjudication call, merged in code
proposals.why_it_matters: One prompt that both reviews detector output and invents new findings anchors on the detector and overloads the task; the result is restatements. Separating discovery from adjudication is supported by impeccable's isolation rule and UICrit's task-overload finding, and it lets the code merge corroborated items.
proposals.test: Call A (discover): digest without detector findings, schema add[] and notReviewed only. Call B (adjudicate): digest slice for elements that carry detector findings plus those findings, schema suppress[] and rewrite[] and brief only. Run in parallel; each <= 2,000 output tokens (within the existing 4,096 cap). Code merge: an A add on the same el and same rule family (keyword or Jaccard >= 0.6) as a detector finding is tagged corroborated and ranked up and not displayed twice; other A adds go through A4-03/A4-04; B's brief is generated from merged results. local-cli providers fall back to a single combined call. Adopt only if an A/B eval shows novel share (adds on elements with no detector finding) improves by >= 15 percentage points versus the single call and the ungrounded drop rate worsens by <= 5 points; otherwise keep the single call.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Evidence for isolation is a methodological rule (impeccable) and an observed quality drop when combining tasks (UICrit), not a measurement of this exact configuration, so it ships behind the eval gate. Cost doubles input tokens; skip call B when there are no detector findings.

proposals.title: Coverage disclosure and downgrade of page-wide absence claims when the digest is partial
proposals.why_it_matters: A budget-trimmed or partly scrolled page looks complete to the model. Without disclosure it will claim things are missing 'across the page' and users will believe a partial review.
proposals.test: digest.coverage carries scrollSteps, finalHeight, infiniteScroll, notScannedBelowPx, omittedElements, omittedSections, hiddenByOpacity. If omittedElements > 0, infiniteScroll is true, or cross-origin iframes were skipped, then AI findings whose title+detail match /\b(no|none|never|nowhere|missing|lacks?|without|absent)\b.*\b(page|site|anywhere|across|any)\b/i are downgraded to low and tagged 'partial coverage', and are dropped if they assert a count not present in the census. UI line: 'Scanned N viewports to Ypx; X of Y elements omitted by budget; not reviewed: ...' using coverage plus the model's notReviewed. Pass: fixture with 600 eligible elements shows omittedElements = eligible - kept, absence claims downgraded, and notReviewed rendered.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Absence claims about things the census explicitly counts over all elements (for example 'h1 count = 0') remain valid because the census is computed before trimming (A4-01). Do not downgrade claims scoped to a cited element.

proposals.title: Style-census facts for the AI: accent hue count, type-scale ratios, spacing grid share, sibling consistency
proposals.why_it_matters: Palette discipline, hierarchy and consistency are what a model can judge well when given exact aggregates, and are hard to judge from a findings list. These facts replace guessing from pixels and can later back deterministic rules.
proposals.test: Compute over all visible elements before trimming: accentHueCount = number of 28-degree hue bins with painted-area share >= 3%, counting only colors with saturation >= 0.30 and lightness 0.20-0.90 from backgrounds, borders and text, excluding img/svg/video/canvas pixels; typeScale = sorted distinct font sizes with consecutive ratios and minRatio; spacingOnGridShare = share of distinct padding/margin/gap px values divisible by 4 (or 8); siblingConsistency = for groups of >= 3 sibling elements with the same tag and class signature, the share with identical (border-radius, padding, border, box-shadow) tuples and the list of deviants. Provide as census lines; flag in the digest when accentHueCount >= 4, minRatio < 1.125, or siblingConsistency < 0.8 with >= 1 deviant. Pass: a fixture with known colors and sizes yields exact counts and flags.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Exclude status colors (red/green/amber at <= 5% area on role alert/status or class matching /error|success|warning|danger/), logos, and pages where a chart (canvas or svg) covers >= 20% of the area. The accent-hue threshold of 4 is deliberately looser than Gesso's 'more than two' heuristic (S8, a small repo) to reduce false positives, and all cutoffs need calibration on real pages.

proposals.title: Identical-section-cadence detector rule (structural sameness)
proposals.why_it_matters: Runs of near-identical sections (three-up icon cards repeated down the page) are a recognized generated-landing structure that no existing rule covers; the section signatures built for the digest make it computable.
proposals.test: Sections = direct children of main (or body) with height >= max(240px, 25% of viewport height). Signature = [layout (grid|flex|block), column count (distinct left edges of grandchildren within +/-8px, capped 1-4), first heading level, hasMedia (img/svg/video >= 120px), ctaCount bucket (0,1,2+), textBucket (<80, <300, >=300 chars)]. Flag when a run of >= 4 consecutive sections shares an identical signature AND >= 3 of them contain a 3- or 4-card row (children width within +/-2px, height within +/-8%) where each card has one heading and <= 30 words of paragraph text. Severity low, report the first section's element and the run length.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip docs, pricing tables, product listings and changelog pages (>= 6 identical cards inside one grid, or role=list/table semantics, or URL path matching /docs|pricing|changelog|blog/). Require headings to differ in text. Thresholds are this proposal's own; sources only establish structural sameness and repeated-component consistency as judged tells, so ship as low severity and calibrate on a labelled page set before enabling by default.

proposals.title: Audit-tab transparency UI: preview what is sent, grounded chips, dropped counts, optional annotated screenshot
proposals.why_it_matters: Users must be able to see and approve what leaves the browser, and must be able to distinguish verified AI rows from measured detector rows. Showing the drop count keeps trust honest without hiding the AI's misses.
proposals.test: (1) 'Preview what is sent' disclosure shows the redacted digest text, size in chars and estimated tokens, redaction and injection-flag counts, and a SHA-256 of the page-derived payload; test that the hash of the preview equals the hash of the request's page-derived part. First send per origin requires a click. (2) Each AI row shows a chip 'e17 + quoted evidence'; clicking highlights the element via the registry (A4-02). (3) Line under the AI results: 'AI proposed N; K grounded; D dropped (not on page)' with D = N - K. (4) Coverage line from A4-11. (5) Screenshot is off by default; when enabled it is viewport-only after the scroll pass, long edge <= 1568 px (cost = ceil(w/28)*ceil(h/28) visual tokens, <= 1,568 on the standard tier), with numbered e-id labels drawn on the top 12 elements by area so the model correlates pixels to ids; the model is never asked for boxes or coordinates. Pass: UI test asserts preview-hash equality, D = N - K, default screenshot flag false, and that every AI row either resolves its id or is labelled page-level.
proposals.false_positive_guards: No automatic sending; AI rows are visually distinct from measured detector rows. The screenshot toggle warns that screenshots can capture secrets (autofilled fields, visible tokens) and that rendered text can carry injected instructions. The annotated-label overlay is drawn on a copy of the image, never on the live page. Image token figures depend on the provider tier; local providers may differ.

gaps: Digest size budgets (24,000 chars, 180 elements, 24 sections, 60 findings, 40 outline lines) are estimates built from verdict (160 entries per viewport, 48-char labels) and browser-use (100-char text); no token counts were measured against Pixelpush's real providers. The 3.5 chars/token figure is an assumption.

Pixelpush's working tree is mid-edit (extension/background.js and extension/panel/panel.js are modified). The enrichment validator in the working tree already accepts category, refs, evidence and slices adds to 8, while docs/ai-providers.md says up to ten. I did not read detect.js internals beyond grepping for globals and scroll code. Whether its DOM walk can be reused to build the digest cheaply, and how its existing visual-contrast scroll helper near line 5281 overlaps with A4-05, is unverified.

The GitHub search API hit rate limits and multi-word sorted queries returned empty, so repository discovery leaned on single-term queries and direct inspection of known candidates. I may have missed relevant projects.

No open-source DOM-grounded LLM design-critique project with >= 100 stars was found. The closest, apatureai/verdict, has 1 star and no published results (relaxed screen); Gesso-Build/skills has 93 stars (relaxed). Their ideas are unproven outside their own tests.

Quoted numbers (13.1% valid, IoU values, image token formula, 1250/2500 px) come from those summaries and were not re-verified against the primary PDFs. The structured-outputs page was read only up to 100,000 of 105,723 characters.

Thresholds with no source behind the exact number are this proposal's own and need calibration on a labelled fixture set: severity cutoffs (5% area, 3 elements), accentHueCount >= 4, section-run length >= 4, Jaccard 0.6, suppress cap 25%, entropy 3.5 bits/char, scroll step 0.8 viewport.

Ideas only (AGPL, 60 stars = relaxed). Scrolls min(0.1*clientHeight,30)px every 75ms with behavior:auto; stops when scrollY+innerHeight is unchanged for 3 checks; aborts if location.pathname changes; waits longer as more height segments appear; uses document.scrollingElement||body (null-guarded); probe-scrolls to 98% and waits 500ms to test whether the page reacts to scrolling.

Skips lazy-load pass when scrollY already >= pageHeight-1.5*innerHeight; flips [loading=lazy] to eager then restores; spoofs innerHeight/clientHeight and wraps IntersectionObserver to synthesise intersections (needs document_start hooks); end detection via MutationObserver on src/srcset attribute changes plus idle timers (MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_CALLS=10); delegates timers to background to dodge throttling.

Relaxed: last commit 78 days ago. Defaults offset 120, duration 400, once:false, throttle 99ms; position-based: adds aos-animate when scrollY >= elementTop-innerHeight+offset and REMOVES it again when scrolled back above that point unless once:true, so restoring scroll to the top re-hides below-fold content.

Not a public source. Shows settlePage() already exists (maxMs 6000, maxSteps 48, maxViewports 30, stepRatio 0.8, stepDelayMs 130, bottomWaitMs 350, instant scroll, user-input interrupt, restore) and runs BEFORE scan(); isRenderedForBrowserRule drops any element with an ancestor opacity<=0.01; loop tracks intended y rather than actual scroll position.
Chrome loads loading=lazy images within 1250px (4G) or 2500px (3G or lower) of the viewport; do not lazy-load images likely in the initial viewport, especially LCP; omitted width/height worsen CLS.
ScrollToOptions.behavior: smooth | instant | auto; auto defers to computed scroll-behavior, so html{scroll-behavior:smooth} animates plain scrollTo; instant always jumps.
Applies to scrolling boxes; on root it targets the viewport, on body it does not propagate; affects CSSOM scrolling APIs and anchor navigation; user scrolls unaffected; UAs may ignore.

content-visibility:auto skips layout/paint of off-screen subtrees that stay in DOM/a11y tree; contain-intrinsic-size (auto keyword) supplies placeholder size; contentvisibilityautostatechange fires when skipping starts/stops.

Off-screen content-visibility:auto elements get size containment: without contain-intrinsic-size they are 0 height and the scrollbar shifts as sections render; auto keyword remembers last rendered size.

checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true}) returns false while an element is skipped by content-visibility:auto; opacityProperty/visibilityProperty options (legacy aliases checkOpacity/checkVisibilityCSS); Baseline since 2024-03.

Intersection processing is a substep of 'Update the rendering' (needs a frame) and entries are queued only when isIntersecting/threshold state differs from the previous sample, so an element that enters and leaves between two samples is never reported; rootMargin grows/shrinks the root box.

Resumption steps run when the lazy loading attribute is set to Eager 'which causes the element to continue loading'; otherwise a lazy-load IntersectionObserver with implementation-defined margin triggers them.

Visible pages: timers essentially unthrottled; hidden pages: once-per-second timer checks, intensive once-per-minute after 5 min hidden: a sweep driven by setTimeout in a hidden tab runs at ~1 step/s and never gets rendering opportunities.
MV3 service worker is stopped after 30s idle or a single request/event taking >5 min; extension API calls/events reset timers: an executeScript call awaiting the sweep should stay well under 30s.

world:'MAIN' shares the page's JS environment (page scripts can observe/dispatch events); executeScript waits for a returned promise per frame; injected function is serialized; main frame result is first.
SC 2.2.2 (A): moving/scrolling content that starts automatically, lasts >5s and sits beside other content needs a pause/stop/hide mechanism; five seconds chosen as long enough to get attention.

SC 2.3.3 (AAA): interaction-triggered motion animation can be disabled; parallax named as typical; 'moving new content into the viewport is essential for scrolling'; techniques C39 (prefers-reduced-motion CSS) and SCR40.

Scroll anchoring is on by default and adjusts scroll position to minimise content shifts, so a requested offset can differ from the actual one after lazy content above resizes (MDN states the mechanism; the programmatic-effect reading is my inference).
