At the bottom require 2 consecutive 300ms windows with scrollHeight delta <=2px (existing bottomWaitMs 350 is kept as the first window). Current settlePage uses a fixed 130ms pause with no frame wait.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Pages with perpetual churn (tickers, autoplay carousels, live regions, video/canvas) never go quiet, so the 700ms per-step cap and the global maxMs bound the cost; ignore mutations inside [aria-live], video, canvas, .audit-*/[id^=audit-live-] and class/style mutations on elements farther than 1 viewport away; resource entries only extend the wait, never fail the scan.
proposals.why_it_matters: vanilla-lazyload (cancel_on_exit default) resets images that leave the viewport before finishing and lazysizes/AOS only evaluate every 99-125ms, so a 130ms hop can leave images/sections unrealised while the scan believes the sweep succeeded; every audited framework (browserless readiness, SingleFile idle, Crawlee network quiet) waits on a quiet signal rather than a constant.

proposals.title: Retune the sweep into a full algorithm: step 0.65H, exact-bottom landing, caps, container detection, restore, cancel
proposals.test: ALGORITHM (delta to settlePage, constants measurable): (0) PRECHECK skip with stats.skipped='hidden' if document.visibilityState!=='visible'; if matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches use profile 'minimal' (step 0.9H, no bounce, no animation-finish wait); record origin {x,y} of every scroller plus an anchor (element at x=vw/2,y=8 and its rect.top) used to correct restore if scrollHeight changed >5%. (1) CONTAINER primary = document.scrollingElement (null-guard quirks mode) if scrollHeight-clientHeight >= max(40, 0.15*innerHeight); else tallest overflowY in {auto,scroll,overlay} with overflow >=200px and area >=0.35*vw*vh. (2) INSTANT set html.style.setProperty('scroll-behavior','auto','important') and always call scrollTo({top,behavior:'instant'}) (el.scrollTo for inner scrollers, not scrollTop=). (3) STEP step=clamp(round(0.65*clientHeight),240,900); next=min(y+step, scrollHeight-clientHeight) so the last stop lands exactly on the bottom (handlers test |scrollTop-(docH-winH)|<=1). (4) DWELL per p1. (5) STOP when: bottom reached and 2 quiet 300ms windows with height delta<=2px; OR stall rule p5; OR caps: 60 steps, 30 viewports and <=20000px, soft 6000ms plus up to 3000ms hard for quiet waits (total <=9s, well under the 30s service-worker idle limit); OR infinite-feed: >=3 growth events (>=0.5H each) observed while parked at the bottom; OR cancel (p9/p13). Once per scan, if no growth at bottom, bounce scrollBy(-0.25H) then back to bottom to re-arm sentinels (Crawlee scrollDownAndUp). (6) AFTER second pass p6, finish animations p4, pin p3, restore origin of every scroller with behavior:'instant' (skip restore if the user interrupted), restore html scroll-behavior and any loading attributes, wait 2xrAF+150ms, then scan(); unpin in finally.
proposals.false_positive_guards: No findings are emitted by the sweep itself; risk is only time and side effects. Keep restore in finally{} so exceptions/cancel still restore; skip restore when a trusted user input interrupted; keep every style/attribute change reversible (record previous inline value+priority).
proposals.why_it_matters: Existing 0.8H steps leave no margin for IntersectionObserver reveals using negative rootMargin (-10% to -20%) with threshold 0.2-0.5 (visible window length is 0.8H+(1-2r)h, equal to the step at r=0.5), 48x130ms exceeds its own 6s budget, and only the first scroller is handled; the parameter set above is the intersection of what browserless/crawl4ai/mrcoles/Lighthouse use, bounded for a side-panel UX.

proposals.title: Pin reveal-on-scroll elements in their revealed state for the scan (once:false libraries re-hide on restore)
proposals.test: Pre-sweep, at origin: build set R (cap 300, outermost only) from body.querySelectorAll('*') (scan cap 6000) of elements with computed opacity<=0.05, display!=='none', no [hidden]/[inert]/aria-hidden=true ancestor, rect area>=400px2, document-top (rect.top+scrollY) > origin viewport bottom (below the fold), and textContent.trim().length>=1 or containing img/svg/video. At each sweep stop after the p1 quiet wait: for e in R not yet seen, if rect intersects the viewport and parseFloat(getComputedStyle(e).opacity)>=0.9 add to WeakSet revealed. After restoring scroll and before scan(): for each e in revealed whose computed opacity is now <0.9, set inline opacity:1, transform:none, visibility:visible all !important (store previous inline value+priority) and increment stats.pinned; remove all pins in finally after findings are serialised. Currently isRenderedForBrowserRule() skips any element with an ancestor opacity<=0.01, so a re-hidden section is invisible to every browser rule.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Only pin elements the page itself revealed (>=0.9) while intersecting the viewport during our sweep, never elements that stayed hidden (tab panels, closed modals, carousel slides, cookie banners, honeypots); skip aria-hidden/inert/hidden/display:none; skip .audit-* nodes; elements inside the user's restored viewport are left alone because the library re-reveals them itself; cap 300 pins; always unpin in finally including on abort.
proposals.why_it_matters: AOS (once:false default) removes aos-animate when scrollY drops below an element's trigger and Motion whileInView animates both ways unless once:true, so the current sequence sweep -> restore -> scan re-hides the content the sweep just realised; scanning at the bottom instead was rejected (header/scrolled-state drift), so pinning is the only way to get both the revealed content and the user's original header/viewport state.

proposals.title: Settle finite CSS animations/transitions (Playwright pattern) before scan instead of a fixed 180ms wait
proposals.test: Before scan() (after restore and p1 quiet wait): for a of document.getAnimations() (cap 400): skip if !a.effect || a.playbackRate===0; skip if a.timeline is a ScrollTimeline/ViewTimeline instance (typeof ScrollTimeline!=='undefined' && a.timeline instanceof ScrollTimeline); skip if effect.target.closest('.audit-overlay,[id^=audit-live-]'); end=a.effect.getComputedTiming().endTime; if Number.isFinite(end) && end<=3000 then try{a.finish()}catch{}. Leave infinite animations untouched (do not cancel, unlike Playwright). Then await 2xrAF; fallback Promise.race([Promise.allSettled(finite.map(a=>a.finished)), sleep(800)]).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip scroll-driven timelines (cannot be finished, progress with scroll, s32); wrap each finish() in try/catch; do not touch infinite animations; 3000ms end-time ceiling avoids fast-forwarding long hero loops; Pixelpush's own overlay animations excluded; elements revert to their post-animation style which is exactly what a user sees once the animation ends.
proposals.why_it_matters: Reveal transitions are typically 400-1000ms (AOS default 400ms; ScreenshotOne waits 400ms per section) so computed opacity/transform at measure time can still be mid-flight, which skews contrast, overflow and layout rules; Playwright's screenshotter shows the production-tested way to land finite animations in their end state.

proposals.title: Read back the real scroll position and stop on stall (blocked, clipped or jacked scrolling)
proposals.test: After each dwell set y = getTop() (actual) instead of the intended value; moved = actual - prevActual; if moved < 0.25*step while actual < (scrollHeight-clientHeight-2) increment stall else reset; stop at stall>=3 with stats.blocked=true (skip bottom waits and restore, nothing moved). Also record stats.drift++ when |actual-intended|>0.5*step (scroll anchoring or mandatory scroll-snap re-snapping). Current loop sets stable=0 and steps++ whenever next>y+1 using the intended y, so with overflow:clip, body scroll locks, wheel-jacked shells or snap-back it burns the whole ~6s budget and reports scrolled:true.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Smooth scroll is neutralised by behavior:'instant' (p2); forward jumps from scroll-snap count as movement; scroll anchoring that moves less than 0.25*step three times in a row while not at the limit is genuinely not progressing; stall counter resets on any qualifying move.
proposals.why_it_matters: Practitioner and crawler code converge on observed-position stall detection (unchanged x3) rather than trusting scrollHeight or intended offsets; the local loop cannot detect a page that ignores scrollTo, so it wastes the scan budget and reports false coverage.

proposals.title: Targeted second pass for unresolved lazy images/iframes and still-skipped content-visibility:auto subtrees
proposals.test: After the main sweep, before restore, build U (cap 16) from: (a) img with (!complete || (complete&&naturalWidth===0&&!currentSrc)) AND (loading==='lazy' or has data-src|data-srcset|data-lazy-src|data-original) AND rect area>=1600px2; (b) iframe[loading=lazy] with rect area>=1600px2; (c) any element with computed contentVisibility==='auto' and el.checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true})===false. For each u: u.scrollIntoView({block:'center',inline:'nearest',behavior:'instant'}), run the p1 quiet wait capped at 500ms; if still !complete and loading==='lazy' set u.loading='eager' (record, restore to 'lazy' afterwards) and wait <=500ms more. Sub-budget 2500ms total, bounded by remaining hard budget.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip display:none or box-less elements (nothing to scroll to); skip images with complete&&naturalWidth===0&&currentSrc (genuinely broken, already reported by broken-image); skip <1600px2 tracking pixels; restore loading attributes; skip entirely if interrupted/blocked.
proposals.why_it_matters: A forward sweep can miss items that vanilla-lazyload cancelled on exit or that content-visibility:auto still skips (descendants have no layout so rect-based rules see zero boxes); revisiting only the unresolved handful with scrollIntoView(instant) and the HTML-spec lazy->eager resumption is cheap and bounded.

proposals.title: Late-hydrating SPA shell wait before concluding 'nothing to scroll'
proposals.test: In the existing early-return branch (scrollHeight-clientHeight < 40): if document.readyState!=='complete' OR body element count < 30 OR a mount node (#root,#app,#__next,#__nuxt,app-root) has childElementCount<=2, poll every 100ms for up to min(1200ms, maxMs/4) until findPrimaryScroller() reports overflow>=40 (document or inner) and its scrollHeight is equal on 2 consecutive polls; then continue the sweep, otherwise exit as today.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Fully loaded short pages (readyState complete, >=30 elements, no empty framework root) skip the wait, so static 404/login pages pay nothing; wait is hard-capped at 1200ms and counts against maxMs.
proposals.why_it_matters: Scans started while an app is still hydrating see a viewport-sized shell and return immediately, auditing an empty skeleton; browserless waits up to 1s for the SPA scroller and polls height stability for exactly this case.

proposals.title: Sweep secondary vertical scroll containers (feeds, inner panes) in addition to the primary scroller
proposals.test: After the primary sweep collect candidates: computed overflowY in {auto,scroll,overlay}; scrollHeight-clientHeight >= max(200, 0.5*clientHeight); clientWidth*clientHeight >= 0.15*vw*vh; rect intersects the viewport or lies within 1 viewport below it; tag not in {TEXTAREA,SELECT,PRE,CODE,INPUT}, no [contenteditable], role not in {listbox,combobox,menu,tree}, not inside .audit-*; and (>=6 element children OR contains img[loading=lazy],[data-src]). Rank by area, take <=2, sweep each with the p2 step/dwell/stop rules (el.scrollTo({top,behavior:'instant'}), end test scrollTop+clientHeight>=scrollHeight-10), sub-budget 1500ms each from the remaining budget, and restore each scrollTop/scrollLeft. Today findPrimaryScroller returns the document whenever it overflows by >40px and ignores every inner container.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Code blocks, tables, text inputs and menus are excluded by tag/role; nav sidebars with >=6 children are swept harmlessly; max 2 containers and 1500ms each bound the cost; skip all when interrupted or the document sweep was blocked.
proposals.why_it_matters: Dashboards, chat/feeds, modals and docs sites keep lazy content in inner overflow panes; Motion's viewport.root option and crawl4ai's container mode exist precisely because IntersectionObserver reveals key off those panes, and the document-level sweep never moves them.

proposals.title: Hardening: abort on hidden tab, navigation or pagehide; count only trusted user input
proposals.test: Each iteration: (1) abort with stats.skipped='hidden' if document.visibilityState!=='visible' (setTimeout runs at ~1/s in hidden pages and IntersectionObserver gets no rendering opportunities); (2) abort without restore if location.pathname+location.search differs from the value at start (SPA route change) or on 'pagehide'; (3) register the interrupt listeners (wheel,touchstart,keydown,mousedown, plus pointerdown) with capture:true,passive:true and set interrupted only when event.isTrusted===true; (4) also listen to 'visibilitychange'. Keep total executeScript wall time <=9s (service worker idle limit is 30s).
proposals.false_positive_guards: isTrusted filter prevents page scripts or carousels that dispatch synthetic wheel/mousedown/keydown from cancelling the scan; ignore modifier-only keydown (Shift/Control/Alt/Meta); navigation abort compares only path+query (ignore hash changes caused by scroll-spy).
proposals.why_it_matters: Existing listeners accept any event, so a page-dispatched synthetic event aborts the sweep and, worse, suppresses restore logic, while a hidden tab silently produces a no-op sweep; MAIN-world code shares the page's event loop and can be influenced by page scripts.

proposals.title: Surface sweep coverage (and feed classification) to the panel and to the AI digest
proposals.test: Return from settlePage and add to the digest/panel: coverage={scroller:'document'|selector, secondary:n, scrolledPx, pageHeightStart, pageHeightEnd, viewport, complete: scrolledPx+viewport>=pageHeightEnd-2, stoppedBy:'bottom'|'time'|'steps'|'viewports'|'distance'|'interrupted'|'blocked'|'hidden'|'navigated'|'feed', feed: growthEvents>=3 || pageHeightEnd/pageHeightStart>=2.5 ? 'infinite':'finite', pinned:n, lazyUnresolved:n}. growthEvent = scrollHeight grows >=0.5*viewport while parked at the bottom (not mid-sweep growth). After the 3rd growth event stop sweeping. Prompt rule for the AI step: absence of findings below scrolledPx or when complete=false is 'unknown', never 'clean'; cite coverage.stoppedBy when asked about below-the-fold sections.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Metadata only; feed classification uses growth observed at the bottom so legitimately long, progressively rendered pages (content-visibility sections) are not mislabelled; cap distance semantics (20000px) reported as stoppedBy:'distance' rather than 'feed'.
proposals.why_it_matters: The AI enrichment sees only detector findings, so a truncated sweep looks identical to a clean page; browserless returns hydrated/scrolledPx/pageHeight and crawl4ai/Crawlee expose step and height caps for exactly this reason; the local stats object already has hitCap/interrupted but nothing consumes it.

proposals.title: Rule lcp-image-lazy: largest above-the-fold image carries loading=lazy
proposals.test: Evaluate at the ORIGINAL scroll position before the sweep (skip rule if origin scrollY > 0.5*innerHeight). Among img elements with display!=='none', visibility visible, no ancestor opacity<=0.01, rect.top+scrollY < innerHeight and rect.bottom>0, rect area >= max(60000px2, 0.10*innerWidth*innerHeight): take the largest by area; flag when img.getAttribute('loading')==='lazy' (also flag fetchpriority='low'). Pair with the loader fix from p6 (do not eager-flip before measuring).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Require visible-in-viewport rect plus opacity/visibility checks so images in hidden carousel slides, tabs or closed menus are ignored; ignore images under the area threshold (icons, avatars); skip if the largest in-viewport image is a CSS background (no loading attribute); skip when origin scroll is deep; one finding per page at most.
proposals.why_it_matters: Official guidance and Lighthouse (lcp-discovery-insight replaces lcp-lazy-loaded) both call lazy-loading the LCP image a measurable defect; it is attribute+rect detectable with near-zero false positives. Frequency on generated pages that blanket-add loading=lazy is my inference, not a cited statistic; both sources are Google so corroboration is not independent.

proposals.title: Rule smooth-scroll-no-reduced-motion: html scroll-behavior:smooth with no prefers-reduced-motion guard
proposals.test: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollBehavior==='smooth' AND no readable stylesheet contains a CSSMediaRule whose conditionText matches /prefers-reduced-motion\s*:\s*reduce/ with a nested style rule setting scroll-behavior to anything but smooth, AND the smooth declaration is not itself inside a CSSMediaRule matching /prefers-reduced-motion\s*:\s*no-preference/ (Tailwind motion-safe compiles to that form). Severity low/info (WCAG 2.3.3 is AAA; C39 is the sufficient technique).
proposals.false_positive_guards: If any stylesheet throws SecurityError on cssRules (cross-origin) and the smooth declaration cannot be located, downgrade to informational or skip; skip when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches and computed value is already auto; do not apply to body (does not propagate to the viewport) or to non-scrolling boxes; ignore scroll-behavior on elements with no overflow.
proposals.why_it_matters: html{scroll-behavior:smooth} is a very common copy-paste snippet; it also silently breaks naive programmatic scanners (animated scrollTo) which is why the sweep forces instant, and it is the one reduced-motion defect detectable from the stylesheet without user interaction. Independent W3C, MDN and Google sources agree on the guard; real-world frequency is an inference.

proposals.title: Panel Cancel button and minimal-motion profile for prefers-reduced-motion users
proposals.test: (a) While progress phase==='scrolling' for >800ms, show a Cancel button next to 'Scrolling the page to load everything... N%'; click sends a message that sets cancelled=true in the MAIN-world sweep (same handling as trusted user input: stop, restore position, continue to scan() on the DOM as it is). Today the panel only shows the percentage. (b) At scan start read matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches in the MAIN world; when true run profile 'minimal' (step 0.9H, no bounce, shorter dwell floor 120ms, show a one-line notice 'Reduced motion: scrolling kept minimal'), and if the autoScroll setting was never explicitly saved default it to off with a one-click 'Scroll to load everything' action.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Cancel never discards findings (scan continues); explicit user setting always overrides the reduced-motion default; sweep stays under ~9s hard so WCAG 2.2.2's 5-second/'mechanism' intent is met by Cancel plus interrupt.
proposals.why_it_matters: The sweep moves the user's page visibly (and triggers site reveal animations) for several seconds; WCAG 2.2.2 expects a way to stop auto-started movement beside other content and web.dev/WCAG treat reduced-motion as the OS-level signal. The 2.3.3 text itself says moving new content into view is essential for scrolling, so this is a courtesy/UX judgement, not a violation claim.

proposals.title: Rule content-visibility-auto-no-intrinsic-size: skipped subtree collapses and jumps on first render
proposals.test: Pre-sweep, for elements with computed contentVisibility==='auto' (scan cap 200, via getComputedStyle) record H0=rect.height and skipped0=!el.checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true}). After the sweep record H1. Flag when computed containIntrinsicBlockSize==='none' (i.e. no contain-intrinsic-size or only 'none') AND skipped0===true AND |H1-H0|>=100px (or H0<32px and H1>=200px).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip elements with contain-intrinsic-size 'auto <length>' or any explicit length; skip elements already rendered at scan start (skipped0 false) so near-viewport sections never flag; require measured height change, not just the property; cap 200 candidates; one finding per page listing the first 3 selectors.
proposals.why_it_matters: Without a placeholder size the box is 0px tall until rendered and the scrollbar/layout jumps; the sweep gives a free before/after height measurement. Real-world frequency is low (inference), so it is ranked last despite near-zero false positives.

gaps: IMPORTANT CONTEXT: the uncommitted working tree already contains settlePage() (extension/audit/detect.js ~L5679-5826: maxMs 6000, maxSteps 48, maxViewports 30, stepRatio 0.8, stepDelayMs 130, bottomWaitMs 350, instant scroll, trusted-agnostic interrupt listeners, restore, panel progress text) plus an autoScroll panel toggle. Every proposal above is a delta against that code, not a greenfield sweep; it was found mid-research after reading antipatterns.json.

GitHub repo search (30/min shared limit) was exhausted early, so discovery of niche autoscroll repos was thin; finalists were chosen by known-name direct lookups plus a few qualifier searches. Dozens of full-page-screenshot extension repos had <15 stars and were not inspected.

No empirical measurement on real sites: thresholds (0.65H, 160ms floor, 700ms cap, 300 pins, 9s hard cap) are derived from source constants and spec reasoning, not benchmarked. Recommend a fixture suite: AOS once:false page, Motion whileInView page, vanilla-lazyload with cancel_on_exit, lazysizes, native loading=lazy, content-visibility:auto, app-shell inner scroller, infinite feed (scrapy-playwright scroll.html), scroll-lock body, html{scroll-behavior:smooth}.

AOS source relied on is stale (default branch last commit 2018) and Motion docs were read only from the public docs page (amount/margin defaults were not shown); verify the re-hide behaviour against the current AOS and Motion releases before shipping p3.

Whether mandatory scroll-snap re-snaps after programmatic scrollTo is not stated by the MDN page I fetched (CSS Scroll Snap spec not read); p5 therefore treats it as a stall/drift case detected empirically rather than assuming behaviour.

I could not verify Chrome's exact behaviour of animation.finish() on every CSS-transition/WAAPI combination or on ViewTimeline animations (Playwright wraps it in try/catch for the same reason); p4 skips scroll-driven timelines and swallows exceptions.

Cross-origin and same-origin iframes are not swept (detector runs in the top frame; executeScript allFrames would be needed), horizontal carousels (overflow-x) and virtualized lists that REMOVE offscreen DOM (react-window style, crawl4ai 'replaced' mode) are only audited as whatever is rendered at the end; no incremental harvest-per-stop design was specified.

scan() loops cap at 6000 elements in DOM order (detect.js ~L5424), so after a successful sweep makes the page longer, below-fold content can still be truncated by the cap; this is outside arm 3 but interacts with it (consider viewport-region sampling).

Playwright issue #40941 (full-page capture and unrealised content) was cited only in a search summary and not opened; Chrome Web Store policy text on user-visible scripted scrolling was not consulted; Chrome-specific user-interruption precedents beyond WCAG 2.2.2/2.3.3 were not found in public repos (user-input abort is documented by the local code only).
rejected: Viewport inflation via CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (Lighthouse full-page-screenshot approach, s10): needs chrome.debugger permission and shows the 'debugging this browser' banner; far heavier trust cost than an in-page sweep.

SingleFile-style MAIN-world hook patching (spoof innerHeight/clientHeight, wrap IntersectionObserver, override getBoundingClientRect, s5): must be installed at document_start before page scripts create observers, cannot re-trigger observers created earlier, is detectable/fragile, and is AGPL (ideas only). Only the loading=lazy->eager flip was adopted (p6), reversibly.

Run the audit at the bottom position before restoring scroll: avoids the re-hide for AOS but still re-hides content above the viewport for Motion whileInView and makes sticky/fixed headers audit in their scrolled state (shrunk/opaque) which can create contrast/layout false positives (inference). Replaced by pinning (p3).

Continuous slow smooth scroll (browsertrix 30px per 75ms, ~400px/s): over 20s for an 8000px page, exceeds the 6-9s budget and WCAG 2.2.2's 5-second spirit; its getEventListeners() gating is a DevTools-only API unavailable in page or content-script worlds.

Dispatching synthetic wheel/mouse events to mimic Crawlee's page.mouse.wheel: isTrusted is false, many libraries ignore them, and it needs CDP to be real input; native scrollTo already drives IntersectionObserver and scroll listeners.

crawl4ai virtual-scroll chunk merging (concatenating HTML snapshots of replaced items): produces strings not live DOM; this audit needs live computed styles and rects, so only the container-detection and 'replaced vs appended' idea was kept (gap noted).

Fixed-height page-count loops that measure scrollHeight once (browsertime scroll.toBottom, puppeteer-autoscroll-down 50 stars, most blog snippets): miss growth and infinite feeds; used as negative examples only.

BackstopJS (no built-in lazy scrolling; user scripts only), lost-pixel (archived), Percy scrollToBottom (87 stars, opt-in, no dwell; kept only as corroboration), aFarkas/lazysizes and michalsnik/aos as implementation models (stale; used only for default constants/behaviour evidence).

Hash/anchor scrollIntoView of every section or every heading as the sweep driver: more layout work per target, depends on DOM structure, and misses sections without headings; the step sweep is structure-agnostic.

A standalone rule for 'reveal-on-scroll content stays opacity:0 after the sweep' (WCAG 2.3.3/C39 angle): real hidden-by-default content is indistinguishable from tabs/modals/carousels by computed style alone without the pinning evidence, so false-positive risk is high; revisit after p3 produces revealed/never-revealed telemetry.

arm: ARM 2 - Mature web audit/lint tools and their heuristics (axe-core, Lighthouse, Vercel web-interface-guidelines, Project Wallace css-analyzer family, Stylelint core and stylelint-a11y, webhint, WebAIM/W3C/web.dev docs). Proposals are differential against the CURRENT WORKING TREE of extension/audit/detect.js, not only antipatterns.json. The working tree (uncommitted, about +923 lines) already contains these rules, so they are not re-proposed: missing-alt, input-no-label, small-tap-target, link-not-distinguishable, focus-outline-removed, missing-lang, heading-one, horizontal-overflow, placeholder-copy, uniform-card-grid, stat-row-cliche, glass-overuse, emoji-icons, blob-decor. It also has an autoscroll pass (settlePage) and an AI page digest (buildPageDigest with opaque refs). Where mature tools suggest stricter or different thresholds, the proposal is a refinement of that in-progress code.

sources.observation: target-size: minSize 24; early pass when both dimensions >=240; spacing exception via 12px-radius circle vs neighbours; neighbours count only if focusable widget AND different destination (resolved href equality; '', javascript: and '#' never match); fully obscured targets pass; tabindex<0 targets yield 'incomplete' not fail; inline targets inside a text block are excluded; rule is disabled by default in axe. MPL-2.0: ideas only.

Link passes if fg or bg contrast vs the nearest block ancestor >=3:1 (allowSameColor true) OR elementIsDistinct: background-image!=none, border-top/bottom/outline with style!=none, width>0 and alpha>0, first font-family differs, or text-decoration/weight/style/size differ. ::before/::after content returns 'incomplete'. Text-block test: block parent's non-widget text longer than widget text; display block/list-item/table/flex/grid/inline-block/inline-flex/inline-grid is not in a text block.

Visually-hidden ladder: display none, visibility hidden/collapse, content-visibility hidden on ancestors, details closed, opacity '0', clip rect() with width/height<=0 on absolute/fixed, clip-path inset>=50% or circle(0), overflow-hidden ancestor whose box is <2px or does not overlap, element offscreen (bottom<=0, left/right beyond doc). Note opacity:0 content is treated as hidden, so unrevealed reveal-on-scroll content is silently skipped.

sources.path: lib/rules/image-alt.json; label.json; label-matches.js; link-name.json; button-name.json; no-explicit-name-required-matches.js; page-has-heading-one.json; lib/checks/shared/has-alt-evaluate.js; lib/checks/generic/has-text-content-evaluate.js; lib/checks/mobile/meta-viewport-scale-evaluate.js; doc/rule-descriptions.md
sources.observation: image-alt passes on ANY of alt attr, aria-label, aria-labelledby, non-empty title, presentational role; fails alt=' ' (alt-space-value). link-name: a[href] needs subtree text, aria-label, aria-labelledby or title. button-name adds implicit/explicit label. label: input/textarea (not hidden/image/button/submit/reset) accepts label, aria-label(ledby), title, placeholder, but a hidden explicit label fails. page-has-heading-one only requires >=1 h1 (moderate best-practice); multiple h1 is NOT flagged. meta-viewport: user-scalable=no/0 or maximum-scale<2 fails.

Distortion: only object-fit:fill, svg excluded, natural >5px both dims, compare the smaller derived dimension with THRESHOLD_PX=2. Resolution: skip displayed<=1px, svg, CSS backgrounds, image-rendering pixelated/crisp-edges, srcset density descriptors; small images (both dims <=64px) need factor 1.0 x DPR, larger need 0.75 x DPR; fail if either natural dimension is below expected. Gatherer distrusts naturalWidth for <picture>/srcset and re-measures currentSrc; uses img.width/height as displayed size.

Non-descriptive English link text set: click here, click this, go, here, information, learn more, more, more info, more information, right here, read more, see more, start, this (plus ~10 other languages). crawlable-anchors fails empty href, javascript:void(0), unparseable and file: hrefs; passes when role is set, mailto:, a[id] with empty href, or a non-empty name attr; anchors without href fail only if an event listener exists (listeners read via DOMDebugger, unavailable to page JS).

Runs axe in-page with an explicit rule allowlist (target-size, empty-heading, heading-order enabled; duplicate-id etc. disabled), then resets scrollTop to 0 and restores the original scroll position in a finally block: scan-then-restore is the incumbent pattern.

Evidence node shape: selector, devtools path, boundingRect, outerHTML snippet capped at 500 chars, nodeLabel (innerText, else alt, else aria-label, else first child [alt]/[aria-label]) truncated to 80 chars. Compact, citeable per-finding evidence.

sources.path: core/audits/seo/font-size.js; core/audits/seo/tap-targets.js; core/gather/gatherers/seo/font-size.js (tag v11.7.1, tag object c4a0e2c8...)
sources.observation: HISTORICAL (removed from current main): font-size passed when >=60% of text characters were >=12px; tap-targets used 48px finger size with overlap-score ratio threshold 0.25 and visibility filtering. Both were superseded by axe target-size (24px) in current Lighthouse. Used only for the optional 48px/coarse-pointer tier and to justify not duplicating tiny-text.

Checklist rules relevant here: icon-only buttons need aria-label; never outline:none without a focus replacement; never transition:all; honor prefers-reduced-motion; autoplay motion >5s needs pause; img needs width/height; specific button labels not 'Continue'; flag div/span click handlers; user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1. Opinionated, no numeric thresholds beyond 5s.

Per token class (colors by property context, fontSizes, fontFamilies, lineHeights, borderRadiuses, boxShadows, zindexes) emits total, totalUnique, uniquenessRatio and top values; colors also by format (hex3/6, rgb...). No thresholds shipped. Values are compared as authored strings.

Source-level guards, not rendered design. Portable methodology only: duplicate ratio penalised when uniqueness <66%; 'more than the most common value' guard fires only when >10% of items exceed the mode.

Hue/saturation bucketing of colours: saturation<5 grey; white/black at S<10 and L=100/0; hue bands <22 red, <50 orange, <72 yellow, <144 green, <180 cyan, <250 blue, <300 magenta, <350 pink, else red. EUPL-1.2 and <100 stars: ideas only, relaxed screen.

Generic-fallback rule guards: ignore @font-face, system font keywords, var()/non-standard last value, any generic keyword present anywhere in the list. Inspected and rejected for this product: low design impact.

no-outline-none: a rule whose selector contains :focus and sets outline 0/none passes only if the same rule sets a non-transparent border/border-color/box-shadow. media-prefers-reduced-motion: transition/animation/animation-name require a prefers-reduced-motion override setting them to none. font-size-is-readable threshold 15px. Stale since 2020: rule logic only.

Independent corroboration for viewport rule: error on maximum-scale, minimum-scale, user-scalable; requires width=device-width. button-type: skips template expressions and spread attributes, warns inside forms. Last commit ~100 days old (relaxed). Most other hints are network/headers/manifest and not page-design relevant.

proposals.title: control-missing-name: links, buttons and role widgets with no accessible name (icon-only controls)
proposals.test: For each visible element matching a[href], button, summary, [role=button|link|menuitem|tab|switch|checkbox|radio], compute the accessible name as the first non-empty trimmed value of: aria-labelledby (concatenated text of ids that exist), aria-label, subtree accessible text (visible text + descendant img[alt] non-empty + descendant [aria-label] + svg>title text), title attribute; for input[type=button|submit|reset] use value, for input[type=image] use alt. FAIL when the name is empty. Tier HIGH when the only content is svg/img/i/span rendered with an icon font (computed font-family matches /icon|awesome|material|symbols|glyph/i) or ::before/::after content in U+E000-U+F8FF; tier MEDIUM otherwise. Report the first 10 distinct offenders (dedupe by tag+class signature) plus the total count. Threshold: 1 occurrence is enough (axe parity); escalate to 'warning' at >=3.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip a without href, aria-hidden subtrees, [inert], closed <details>, display/visibility hidden and axe-style visually hidden (clip rect(0,0,0,0), clip-path inset>=50%, box <=2x2px, offscreen bottom<=0/right<=0). Alphabetic ::before/::after content counts as a name (Chrome includes generated content); private-use glyphs do not. Stretched-link cards whose sibling sr-only span supplies text pass because subtree text is non-empty. aria-labelledby pointing to an existing non-empty element passes. img[alt=""] as the only content of a link still fails (axe behaviour). Only the 'name present' decision is made; never judge name quality here.
proposals.why_it_matters: Highest real-world frequency among checks the detector lacks: WebAIM 2026 finds empty links on 46.3% and empty buttons on 30.6% of home pages, and generated UIs ship icon-only buttons constantly. The working tree only checks form fields and img alt, so this whole class (nav hamburgers, social icons, close buttons) is invisible today. Trivial to compute, low FP.

proposals.title: Axe-parity guards for the in-progress missing-alt, input-no-label and heading-one rules
proposals.test: missing-alt: do NOT flag an lacking alt when any of these is present: non-empty trimmed aria-label, aria-labelledby resolving to existing non-empty text, non-empty title (axe image-alt 'any' list). DO add: (a) alt present but whitespace-only on a non-decorative image (axe alt-space-value); (b) advisory when alt matches /\.(jpe?g|png|webp|gif|svg|avif)$/i or /^(img|image|dsc|screenshot)[-_ ]?\d+$/i; (c) svg[role=img] and [role=img] with no /aria-label(ledby); input[type=image] without alt. input-no-label: treat whitespace-only aria-label as unnamed; aria-labelledby with no existing or empty target as unnamed; a <label> that is display:none/visibility:hidden does not count (axe hidden-explicit-label); title-only is advisory (axe label-title-only); placeholder-only stays flagged but one tier lower than 'no name at all'. heading-one: keep the zero-visible-h1 branch (also accept [role=heading][aria-level=1]); remove or downgrade the 'more than one h1' branch to advisory.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Each guard is a pure removal of a false positive except the three additions, which only fire on explicit markup defects. The multi-h1 branch is not a failure in axe (page-has-heading-one needs >=1) and WebAIM reports >1 h1 on 18.1% of pages as a statistic, so flagging it at 'warning' will fire on a large share of legitimate pages. Keep the existing size>=8px guard for tracking pixels.
proposals.why_it_matters: The current missing-alt flags images that axe passes (aria-label/title) and input-no-label accepts dangling aria-labelledby ids, so it both over- and under-reports; the multi-h1 branch likely produces the most common false positive of the new document checks. Fixing precision first protects trust in every other finding.

proposals.title: Visually-hidden and same-target guards for small-tap-target
proposals.test: Before pushing an element into targets[], skip it when: (1) axe clipHidden: computed clip rect() with right-left<=0 and bottom-top<=0 on position absolute|fixed, or clip-path inset(>=50%) / circle(0); (2) box width<=2 and height<=2, or an overflow:hidden ancestor whose box is <2px; (3) offscreen: rect.bottom<=0 or rect.right<=0 for non-fixed elements; (4) pointer-events:none; (5) tabindex=-1 with no widget role; (6) aria-disabled=true; (7) native input[type=checkbox|radio] with computed appearance:auto and no author width/height (user-agent-control exception); (8) fully enclosed by another target's rect (axe: obscured, passes). In the neighbour test, treat two a[href] elements as the SAME target when new URL(href, baseURI).href is equal and the href is not '', 'javascript:' or ending '#'; treat a control and its <label for>/wrapping label as one target. Early exit: if the element is >=240x240 skip neighbour work. Optional second tier (advisory): on (pointer: coarse) or viewport width<=480, primary CTAs below 44px on the short side.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Keep the existing WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception (12px circle vs neighbours, 24px centre distance between two undersized targets). Report tabindex=-1 neighbours as 'incomplete' rather than blocking, as axe does. Never count the extension's own overlays (already filtered by class).
proposals.why_it_matters: isElementHidden uses checkVisibility with checkOpacity:false, which does not see clip/1px sr-only patterns, so Tailwind '.sr-only' skip links (1x1, first in DOM, next to the logo link) and sr-only labels are very likely to be reported as undersized targets. Same-destination image+title card links are also double counted. The 6000-element cap and per-target O(n) neighbour loop get cheaper with the 240px early exit.

proposals.title: Distinctness guards for link-not-distinguishable (custom underlines, nearest block, incomplete state)
proposals.test: Replace the current 'underline or border-bottom or same weight' test with axe's distinctness set evaluated against the NEAREST BLOCK ancestor (not just parentElement): link is distinct if ANY of: background-image != none; border-top/border-bottom/outline with style != none, width > 0, alpha > 0; box-shadow containing an inset offset-y <= -1px and blur 0 (underline trick); first font-family token differs; text-decoration-line or text-decoration-style differ; font-style differs; font-size differs; font-weight differs by >=100. If the link has ::before/::after with content != none and (height <= 3px or position absolute), return INCOMPLETE (do not fail). Otherwise compute relative-luminance contrast of link colour vs block text colour; if >= 3:1 pass; else compute background contrast and pass if >= 3:1; FAIL only when both < 3:1 (colour-identical links also fail unless distinct). Text-block membership: nearest block ancestor's own non-widget text length > total widget (link/button) text length, and link display not in block/list-item/table/flex/grid/inline-block/inline-flex/inline-grid.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Evaluate at rest: hover/focus-only underline still fails (W3C F73), bold or underline passes. Skip links inside nav, footers and list items whose text is mostly links (text-length rule handles this). Skip hidden/visually-hidden links. Pseudo-element decoration and gradient underlines are the dominant false-positive source today and are explicitly routed to pass/incomplete.
proposals.why_it_matters: Animated underlines via a::after, background-image gradients and inset box-shadows are ubiquitous on modern and generated sites; the in-progress rule only recognises text-decoration and border-bottom, so it will flag well-designed links as 'looks like body text'. Compare against the real block colour instead of an inline wrapper (em/strong) to avoid wrong contrast.

proposals.title: focus-indicator-probe: verify a visible focus change by focusing real tab stops (supersedes CSS-text heuristics)
proposals.test: After the main scan (deep mode, last step), take the first N=40 visible, non-disabled elements in tab order (a[href], button, input, select, textarea, summary, [tabindex>=0]; not hidden/clipped; rect >= 1x1). For each: snapshot computed outline-style/width/color/offset, box-shadow, border-top-color/width, background-color, color, text-decoration-line/color, filter, transform; call el.focus({preventScroll:true}); require el.matches(':focus-visible'), else mark INCONCLUSIVE and skip; snapshot again. The element FAILS when none of: (outline-style not none/hidden AND outline-width>0 AND outline alpha>0 AND it changed) or box-shadow changed to non-none with non-transparent colour, or border/background/text-decoration changed. Aggregate by tag+class signature; flag when >=3 elements fail OR >=25% of conclusive probes fail. Always restore (blur, then refocus the previous activeElement). Also keep static checks for patterns the current regex skips: selector containing :focus-visible with outline none/0 and no replacement; global resets (*, a, button, [tabindex] with outline none/0) with no later :focus-visible restore; Tailwind-style 'focus:outline-none' elements with no focus:ring/focus-visible/focus:border/focus:shadow sibling class.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip elements with aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls and form controls inside dialogs (focus handlers may open menus or move focus); skip contenteditable and iframes; wrap in try/catch; run only when no user interaction in the last 2s. Forced-colors outlines count as changes (outline-style auto on focus-visible is a change). Treat transparent outline (Tailwind focus:outline-none leaves 2px solid transparent) as no outline. Cross-origin stylesheets are unreadable to the static scan, which is exactly why the probe is needed; report unreadable-sheet count in coverage.
proposals.why_it_matters: The existing static scan only matches plain :focus selectors, excludes any selector containing a backslash (all utility classes) and is switched off globally if any :focus-visible rule sets an outline, so it misses the most common real pattern (outline-none with no ring) and global resets. A computed-style probe measures the thing WCAG 2.4.7 actually tests (F78: tab to each element and look) and works with CSS-in-JS and cross-origin CSS. Effect on pages: keyboard-focus loss is one of the most common AI-generated-UI defects.

proposals.title: motion-hygiene: transition: all and unbounded motion without a reduced-motion override
proposals.test: (a) transition-all: for each visible element, split computed transition-property on ','; an entry 'all' counts only if the index-aligned (cycled) transition-duration entry is > 0s (the default 'all 0s' must NOT count). Flag when >=3 elements qualify, or any qualifying element has area >= 40,000 px^2; evidence = top 3 selectors. Note existing layout-transition explicitly ignores 'all'. (b) no-reduced-motion: take document.getAnimations() filtered to playState running or pending on visible targets; count CSSAnimation with effect.getComputedTiming().iterations === Infinity OR activeDuration > 5000ms; exclude targets under [role=progressbar], [role=status], [aria-busy=true], and spinner-like animations (animationName /spin|rotate|loader|pulse|shimmer|skeleton/i on boxes < 64x64). Flag when count >= 1 AND no readable CSSMediaRule/MediaList containing 'prefers-reduced-motion' exists in any same-origin stylesheet. If any stylesheet is unreadable (cross-origin SecurityError) downgrade to INCOMPLETE.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Duration guard is mandatory for (a). Do not require (b) for single short opacity fades (<=300ms). Do not flag when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') rules exist but live only in unreadable sheets (incomplete). Canvas/Lottie/video motion is invisible to this check and is out of scope.
proposals.why_it_matters: Only 44.15% of >100k homepages ship any prefers-reduced-motion media query (Project Wallace 2026), and transition-all is the default of utility classes in generated pages. Vercel's guidelines and stylelint-a11y both encode these rules; the detector currently has no signal for either.

proposals.title: placeholder-links: href="#" / javascript:void(0) calls to action
proposals.test: Count visible a elements with no role attribute, not inside [role=tablist|menu|menubar], whose whitespace-stripped href attribute matches /^(#!?|javascript:(void\(?0\)?)?;?)?$/i, with none of: aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-haspopup, data-toggle/data-bs-toggle/data-action/data-target, onclick attribute or property, framework handler markers (React: an own property starting __reactProps$ whose value has onClick; Vue: el._vei with click; attributes starting @, x-on:, v-on:, (click), ng-click). Flag when count >= 3 (page level, report top 5 with nodeLabel), OR when any single match renders as a CTA (opaque background alpha >= 0.5 or border >= 1px, height >= 32px) within the first 1.5 viewport heights.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Skip links to '#id' targets (skip links, in-page anchors) and a[id] without href; skip mailto/tel. Listeners added with addEventListener are invisible to page JS, so require >=3 matches (or a CTA-styled one) and prefer framework markers; Lighthouse itself only fails anchors without href when a listener exists, via a DevTools-only API. SPA routers that use href="#" with delegated handlers can still false-positive: keep severity advisory and let AI enrichment suppress.
proposals.why_it_matters: Dead '#' navigation, footer columns and primary CTAs are a classic generated-mockup tell and a genuine product defect; none of the 60 current rules sees it. Detection is a single attribute read per anchor, so it is cheap. Frequency is not measured in any public source (estimate only).

proposals.title: repeated-generic-link-text: 'Learn more ->' wallpaper and non-descriptive link names
proposals.test: For each visible a[href] / [role=link], build the accessible name (as P01) and normalise: lowercase, trim, strip leading/trailing runs of arrows and punctuation [\s→›»>↗↘⟶…·|\-–—]+, collapse whitespace. Quality tier: normalised name is in the Lighthouse English set {click here, click this, go, here, information, learn more, more, more info, more information, right here, read more, see more, start, this} -> advisory per page (list first 5). Slop tier: >=3 links on the page share the same normalised name from that set and resolve to >=2 distinct URLs or '#' (resolved via the same rules as P07), located in >=3 different container sections -> 'warning' (repeated generic CTA). Secondary: >=3 links with identical normalised name (any text) but different hrefs and no distinguishing aria-label (axe identical-links-same-purpose, minor).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Pass when aria-label, aria-labelledby or a visually hidden suffix (e.g. 'Read more about X') makes the accessible name unique. Skip links inside nav/header/footer link lists and pagination (Next/Previous are not in the set). Do not count buttons. Only use the English set unless document language is declared otherwise; add other Lighthouse language sets keyed by html[lang].
proposals.why_it_matters: Three feature cards each ending in 'Learn more ->' is one of the most recognisable generated-page patterns and also a real accessibility defect (links read out of context). The existing slop rules look at copy cadence and buzzwords but never at link labelling; detection is exact-string and very low FP.

proposals.title: image-render-fidelity: distorted aspect ratio and upscaled (blurry) images
proposals.test: After autoscroll settles, for each visible with complete && naturalWidth>0 (skip otherwise, never flag unloaded lazy images). Natural size: use naturalWidth/Height, but for or srcset-w images re-measure by decoding currentSrc in a detached Image (Lighthouse distrusts naturalWidth there). Displayed size: img.width/img.height (content box, layout px; unaffected by transforms). DISTORTION: only when computed object-fit is 'fill', neither dimension <=5px natural, not svg; r = natW/natH; tH = dispW/r; tW = dispH*r; compare the SMALLER of tH/tW: if tH < tW fail when |tH - dispH| >= 2px, else fail when |tW - dispW| >= 2px. UPSCALE: skip displayed<=1px, svg (currentSrc extension or Content-Type), image-rendering pixelated|crisp-edges, srcset with density descriptors (/ \d+(\.\d+)?x/), CSS backgrounds. dpr = window.devicePixelRatio rounded to nearest 0.5 (min 1). factor = 1.0 if both displayed dims <=64px else 0.75. Fail when natW < ceil(factor*dpr*dispW) OR natH < ceil(factor*dpr*dispH). Report ratio natural/needed and cap at 8 findings.
proposals.false_positive_guards: object-fit cover/contain/scale-down/none and aspect-ratio + cover crops are intentional and skipped. Padding and border are excluded by using img.width/height rather than the border-box rect. Images inside hidden carousels slides (opacity 0 or offscreen) are skipped by the visibility ladder. Report at DPR 1 using the 0.75 factor so desktop scans only flag images visibly soft at 1x. Needs P10 (decode wait) or lazy images will be skipped as unloaded.
proposals.why_it_matters: These are real visible bugs a design reviewer would call out (squashed logos/avatars from width+height set without object-fit; 600px hero images stretched to 1600px). Lighthouse encodes the tolerances after years of tuning, and none of the 60 rules reads naturalWidth against displayed size.

proposals.title: settlePage hardening: verify scroll, wait for lazy images/fonts/reveals, avoid re-hide, lift the 6000-element cap
proposals.test: Keep the existing walk (0.8*viewport, 130ms, 350ms bottom wait, caps 48 steps/30 viewports/6s, instant behaviour, user interrupt, restore) and add measurable gates: (1) step = min(0.8*clientHeight, 1000px) so every lazy image enters Chrome's 1250px (4G) load zone even on tall viewports; (2) after setTop(next) read back getTop(); if |getTop()-next| > 2px on 2 consecutive steps, mark scroller unscrollable (html overflow hidden / snap-driven pages), try the next-largest overflow candidate, else abort after 1s instead of burning the 6s budget and reporting scrolled=true; (3) before measuring: await Promise.race([Promise.allSettled(img.decode() for img.loading==='lazy && !img.complete within +-1500px of the viewport), 1500ms]); await Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, 1000ms]); await Promise.race([Promise.allSettled(finite getAnimations().map(a=>a.finished)), 1200ms]); replace the fixed 180ms pause; (4) re-hide detection: at the bottom record R = text-bearing elements whose computed opacity >= 0.9 now and <= 0.1 at start; after restoring scroll count how many of R are back at <= 0.1; if >0, run scan() BEFORE restoring scroll (then restore); (5) replace the three 'if (++seen > 6000) break' loops (design pass, findPrimaryScroller, digest) with an ordered, time-sliced walk (yield every ~12ms via setTimeout 0) bounded by a time budget (e.g. 800ms per pass), and record visited/total so a cap hit is visible (see P11).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Respect user interruption and never exceed maxMs 15000. Infinite feeds: keep maxViewports (30) and add a height-growth guard (stop if scrollHeight grows >3x initial). Do not auto-click 'load more' buttons. content-visibility:auto subtrees only render when scrolled near, so run (3) after the last step, not before. display:none lazy images never load (web.dev), so they cannot be fixed by scrolling and must be reported as not-evaluated, not broken.
proposals.why_it_matters: The working tree has the right skeleton but would still miss content in four ways: unscrollable-root pages waste 6s, large lazy images are not decoded when measurement starts, toggle-style IntersectionObserver reveals re-hide after scroll-back (axe-style visibility checks skip opacity:0 content, so those sections silently vanish from every rule), and long pages hit the 6000-element hard stop in DOM order, dropping the bottom. Lighthouse also restores scroll in a finally block, so restore semantics are sound.

proposals.title: Scan coverage chip: show what was not evaluated (axe incomplete/inapplicable analogue)
proposals.test: Extend the scan result with coverage = { elementsTotal, elementsVisited, capHit: bool, settle: { steps, hitCap, interrupted, heightBefore, heightAfter, container }, skippedHidden: n (display none, visibility, clip/offscreen per axe ladder), unreadableSheets: n (cross-origin cssRules SecurityError, currently swallowed by try/catch), unrevealed: n (text-bearing elements with computed opacity < 0.05 after settle), imagesNotLoaded: n }. Show a header chip 'Scanned X of Y elements - N stylesheets unreadable - M hidden by opacity' only when elementsVisited/elementsTotal < 0.95 OR capHit OR settle.hitCap OR settle.interrupted OR unreadableSheets > 0 OR unrevealed > 0; hide otherwise. Include coverage (counts only) in the AI digest.
proposals.false_positive_guards: Counts only, no selectors or URLs (privacy parity with the digest). Do not show the chip for pages that simply have few elements. Never label unrevealed content as an error.
proposals.why_it_matters: Right now a cap hit, unreadable CSS or an interrupted scroll silently turns into 'no findings', which users read as 'clean page'. axe and Lighthouse both separate violations from incomplete/not-applicable; surfacing coverage is the same trust mechanism and tells users when to re-scan after scrolling.

proposals.title: token-sprawl: type scale, colour, radius and shadow inventory with calibrated thresholds
proposals.test: Compute from the RENDERED DOM (computed values, so 1rem and 16px and red and #f00 collapse; authored-string counting inflates). TYPE: group visible direct-text elements by computed font-size rounded to 0.5px, weight by direct-text character count; a size is SIGNIFICANT if >=1.5% of characters or >=4 elements. Flag when significant >= 11 (advisory at 9-10), OR >=2 near-duplicate significant pairs (|a-b| <= 1px or ratio <= 1.07, e.g. 15/16, 13/14). If >=50% of significant sizes are fractional (fluid clamp/vw type) raise the threshold to 14. COLOUR: bucket distinct painted colours (text colour, backgrounds with alpha>=0.5, borders >=1px) with the Project Wallace bands (saturation<5 grey; hue <22 red, <50 orange, <72 yellow, <144 green, <180 cyan, <250 blue, <300 magenta, <350 pink); flag when >=5 chromatic buckets are each used by a LARGE surface (>=10,000 px^2 background or heading text) ; and flag 'neutral drift' when >=2 pairs of distinct neutral text colours differ by <=3 HSL lightness points and each covers >=1.5% of characters. RADIUS: distinct non-zero radii (first value, rounded to 1px; >=9999px or >=50% on a near-square = 'full') each used by >=3 elements of >=24x24px; flag when more than 5. SHADOW: distinct non-none, non-inset-only box-shadow strings (px rounded, alpha to 0.05) each used by >=3 elements; flag when more than 5. Report the top values with share, plus distinct/total uniqueness ratio.
proposals.false_positive_guards: All numeric thresholds are INITIAL VALUES and must be calibrated on a labelled corpus (about 30 deliberate and 30 generated pages) before enabling at 'warning': published counts (Almanac 2019 median 40 distinct sizes; Project Wallace 2026 median 47 sizes, 164 colours) are authored-CSS string counts including dead rules and cannot be used directly. Exclude svg, canvas, img, video internals, code/pre, data-visualisation containers (chart/graph classes, role=img) and status badges (<10,000 px^2) from the colour count; skip dashboards/tables-dominated pages for colour. Existing flat-type-hierarchy (too FEW sizes) and design-system-* (needs DESIGN.md) are complementary, not duplicates.
proposals.why_it_matters: The digest already computes distinct sizes/colours/radii but nothing turns them into a deterministic finding, so inconsistency across a page ('every card has a slightly different radius, 14 font sizes') is only reported if the AI notices. This is the standard token-consistency lens of css-analyzer and design-token tooling, adapted to rendered pages. Frequency is high but threshold risk is real, hence rank below the structural rules.

proposals.title: Digest v2: deterministic measured evidence for the AI (tokens, accessibility counts, image fidelity, motion, coverage, review items)
proposals.test: Extend buildPageDigest (budget stays DIGEST_MAX_BYTES 14000, new blocks <= 2000 bytes combined, trimmed first when over budget) with: tokens = { fontSizes, textColors, radii, shadows } each as { distinct, significant, uniquenessRatio = distinct/total, top: up to 6 [{v, share}] } using CHARACTER-weighted share (current sizes counts elements, so single-use values inflate distinctSizes); a11y = { linksUnnamed, buttonsUnnamed, inputsUnlabelled, imgsNoAlt, placeholderLinks, genericLinks, h1, skippedHeadings } from P01/P02/P07/P08; images = { distorted, upscaled, lazyUnloaded } from P09; motion = { transitionAll, infiniteAnimations, reducedMotionRule: true|false|'unknown' } from P06; coverage from P11; review = up to 8 incomplete candidates {ref, rule, reason, measured} each <= 160 bytes. Give every ref a label following Lighthouse's precedence (innerText, else alt, else aria-label, else first descendant [alt]/[aria-label]) truncated to 80 chars through the existing redactDigestText; no outerHTML snippet (keep the current no-HTML privacy rule).
proposals.false_positive_guards: Keep opaque refs and the 'unknown ref is dropped' contract. Redact emails, long tokens and phone numbers (existing). Counts must come from the same functions as the rules so panel numbers and AI numbers cannot disagree. Do not send values of form fields or URLs.
proposals.why_it_matters: The model currently sees structure and rounded top-N statistics but not the measured facts that decide most design judgements (are 11 type sizes significant or incidental, is the missing reduced-motion rule real or unknown, did half the images fail to load). Grounded numbers let the evidence-quote rule in the prompt actually bite and cut hallucinated 'adds'.

proposals.title: Tri-state rule outcomes and AI adjudication of 'incomplete' candidates
proposals.test: Let uncertain rules return incomplete (with a messageKey) instead of fail, following axe: P03 target-size when an overlapping neighbour is non-tabbable or >8 overlapping rects or a fully-obscuring overlay; P04 when pseudo-element decoration exists, a background-image sits under the text, or contrast cannot be resolved; P05 when :focus-visible does not match after programmatic focus; P06 when stylesheets are unreadable; P09 when natural size is untrusted. Put up to 8 incomplete items into digest.review (P13). Extend the response schema with review: [{findingKey|ref, verdict: 'confirm'|'dismiss', evidence}] under the existing rules (ref must exist in the digest, evidence is a <=120-char quote from the digest, otherwise the item is dropped). confirm promotes to a 'warning' finding labelled 'AI-confirmed'; dismiss hides it and stores ignoreValue. Guardrail: for any single rule, if more than 30% of its raw candidates would route to review, demote that rule to advisory instead (the rule is too uncertain to adjudicate).
proposals.false_positive_guards: The AI never creates findings from review items beyond those the detector surfaced; it only chooses confirm/dismiss. Cap tokens by the 8-item budget. Without an AI key, incomplete items stay in a collapsed 'Needs review' list and are excluded from any score.
proposals.why_it_matters: Mature tools get precision by separating 'definitely wrong' from 'cannot tell' (axe returns undefined in at least five target-size situations and for pseudo-content links). Today the detector must guess fail/pass for ambiguous cases and the AI can only suppress or add; routing ambiguity to the AI that actually sees the digest uses it where it adds judgement the detector cannot have.

rejected: Re-proposing missing-alt, input-no-label, small-tap-target, link-not-distinguishable, focus-outline-removed, missing-lang, heading-one, horizontal-overflow, placeholder-copy: rejected, they already exist in the uncommitted working-tree detect.js; only precision guards (P02-P05) were extracted from axe/stylelint-a11y/WCAG.
A fresh autoscroll and AI digest design: rejected as new work because settlePage and buildPageDigest already exist in the working tree; P10, P11, P13, P14 are targeted gaps only.

axe p-as-heading (styled

that looks like a heading: size ratio >=1.4x next paragraph, or weight+150 with size 1.15x, text shorter than 0.5x the next paragraph): experimental in axe, only inspects

; generated pages use styled

titles so FP/FN profile is unvalidated. Dropped to stay within 14.
Lighthouse font-size legibility (>=60% of text chars >=12px): removed from current Lighthouse main and overlaps existing tiny-text; coverage variant adds little.

Lighthouse unsized-images / Vercel 'img needs width and height': performance/CLS rather than visual design; also could not confirm (MDN page silent) that attribute-derived aspect-ratio appears in computed style, so a reliable in-page test needs authored-CSS parsing.
Stylelint font-family-no-missing-generic-family-keyword and time-min-milliseconds: low design impact; icon fonts legitimately omit generic fallbacks.
z-index sprawl (Almanac median 16 distinct, Project Wallace median 18): maintainability only, no visible design effect.

Vercel 'div/span with click handler' and 'buttons need hover state': addEventListener handlers and :hover state cannot be read from page JS, cursor:pointer proxy is too noisy (inherited cursor), CSSOM :hover matching is expensive and CSS-in-JS dependent.
axe color-contrast and scrollable-region-focusable: existing low-contrast rule covers contrast; scrollable regions are low frequency.
Project Wallace css-code-quality scoring (selector counts, @import, file size): source-level CSS metrics, not rendered DOM; only the uniqueness-ratio and mode-outlier methodology was reused.

webhint packages other than meta-viewport/button-type: network, header and manifest hints are out of scope for a rendered-design audit; meta-viewport zoom-lock (user-scalable=no, maximum-scale<2) is deliberately left out of the 14 because it is low frequency and trivial to add from axe/webhint/Vercel (three independent sources agree) if wanted.

cssstats (cssstats/cssstats, 2814 stars, last commit 2023-09-20) and pa11y (LGPL, HTML_CodeSniffer): not inspected at code level; stale or incompatible licence and no thresholds beyond what axe already provides.
gaps: Baseline drift: the brief says the audit does not scroll and AI only sees detector findings, but the working tree (uncommitted, about +923 lines in detect.js, plus panel/background changes) already has settlePage and a digest with refs and a grounded add/suppress prompt. Proposals are differential to that; verify against whatever is committed before implementing.

No public corpus gives rendered-DOM (computed) token distributions. Almanac 2019 and Project Wallace 2026 count authored CSS strings including unused rules, so P12 thresholds (11 significant sizes, 5 radii, 5 shadows, 5 chromatic buckets, 1.07 ratio) are starting guesses that need a labelled calibration run (deliberate vs generated pages) before shipping above advisory. Reference scales I recall (Tailwind 13 sizes, Material 3 about 11 distinct sizes) were not fetched and are unverified.

Behaviour of programmatic element.focus() with respect to :focus-visible was not confirmed (MDN silent; Selectors-4 section 9.4 not retrievable). P05 therefore guards with el.matches(':focus-visible') and treats mismatches as inconclusive; needs a Chrome experiment.
Whether content-visibility:auto descendants return stale or zero getBoundingClientRect before they are scrolled near is not stated by web.dev; P10 assumes they do not render until near the viewport.

WebAIM percentages are share of home pages with at least one WAVE-detected instance, not instance rates, and WAVE is not axe; they rank frequency but do not calibrate FP rates. No public frequency exists for placeholder href="#" links, repeated generic CTAs or link-in-text-block failures.
axe-core is MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft): everything above is behaviour and threshold description only; implement independently. css-design-tokens is EUPL-1.2.

Not executed anywhere: no candidate code was run, no Chrome verification of any proposed test. React/Vue handler-marker checks in P07 (__reactProps$, _vei) are my own technique, not taken from a source, and can break across framework versions.
